title.zh: 卷三百三十四 列傳第九十三 徐禧 李稷 高永能 沈起 劉彝 熊本 蕭注 陶弼 林廣
title.en: Volume 334 Biographies 93: Xu Xi, Li Ji, Gao Yongneng, Shen Qi, Liu Yi, Xiong Ben, Xiao Zhu, Tao Bi, Lin Guang
title.raw: 卷三百三十四 列傳第九十三 徐禧 李稷 高永能 沈起 劉彝 熊本 蕭注 陶弼 林廣 Volume 334 Biographies 93: Xu Xi, Li Ji, Gao Yongneng, Shen Qi, Liu Yi, Xiong Ben, Xiao Zhu, Tao Bi, Lin Guang

sentences.zh: 徐禧，字德占，洪州分寧人。

translations.literal: Xu Xi, style name Dezhan, was a man of Fenning in Hong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xi, whose style name was Dezhan, came from Fenning in Hong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少有志度，博覽周遊，以求知古今事變、風俗利疚，不事科舉。

translations.literal: In youth he had ambition and breadth of mind; he read widely and traveled about to learn the changes of affairs past and present and the benefits and harms of local customs, and did not pursue the civil service examinations.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he was ambitious and far-sighted; he read widely and traveled in search of knowledge about historical change and the strengths and weaknesses of regional customs, and never took the civil service examinations.

sentences.zh: 熙寧初，王安石行新法，禧作《治策》二十四篇以獻。

translations.literal: Early in the Xining reign, when Wang Anshi implemented the New Policies, Xi composed twenty-four essays entitled Policies for Governance and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Xining era, as Wang Anshi was putting the New Policies into effect, Xi wrote twenty-four treatises on statecraft and submitted them to the throne.

sentences.zh: 時呂惠卿領修撰經義局，遂以布衣充檢討。

translations.literal: At that time Lü Huiqing headed the Bureau for Compiling and Revising the Meaning of the Classics, and Xi was appointed reviser as a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Huiqing was then in charge of the bureau that compiled commentaries on the classics, and Xi was brought in as a reviser despite holding no official rank.

sentences.zh: 神宗見其所上策，曰：「禧言朝廷用經術變士，十已八九，然竊襲人之語，不求心通者相半，此言是也。

translations.literal: When the Emperor Shenzong saw the policies he submitted, he said: "Xi says that in using classical learning to transform scholars the court has achieved seven or eight parts in ten, yet those who merely plagiarize others' words without seeking true understanding are about half—this statement is correct.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shenzong read his policy memorials, he remarked, "Xi observes that in reshaping the scholar class through classical learning the court has succeeded in seven or eight cases out of ten, yet half the men involved merely parrot others and never grasp the heart of the matter—he is right about that.

sentences.zh: 宜試於有用之地。」

translations.literal: He should be tried in a post where he can be useful."
translations.idiomatic: He ought to be tested in a position where he can do real work."

sentences.zh: 即授鎮安軍節度推官、中書戶房習學公事。

translations.literal: He was at once appointed military commissioner judge of Zhen'an Army and trainee in the secretariat's household accounts office.
translations.idiomatic: He was immediately given the posts of judicial commissioner of the Zhen'an military commission and trainee in the Secretariat's household accounts section.

sentences.zh: 歲餘召對，顧問久之，曰：「朕多閱人，未見有如卿者。」

translations.literal: After more than a year he was summoned for audience; the emperor gazed at him a long while and said: "I have seen many men, yet never one like you."
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was called in for a private audience; the emperor studied him at length and said, "I have met countless officials, but none like you."

sentences.zh: 擢太子中允、館閣校勘、監察御史裏行。

translations.literal: He was promoted to junior mentor in the heir apparent's palace, collator in the Hanlin archive, and acting investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to junior mentor of the heir apparent, collator in the palace library, and acting investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 與中丞鄧綰、知諫院范百祿雜治趙世居獄。

translations.literal: Together with Vice Censor-in-Chief Deng Wan and Remonstrance Bureau director Fan Bailu he jointly handled the case of Zhao Shiju.
translations.idiomatic: He worked alongside Vice Censor-in-Chief Deng Wan and Fan Bailu, director of the Remonstrance Bureau, on the prosecution of Zhao Shiju.

sentences.zh: 李士寧者，挾術出入貴人間，嘗見世居母康，以仁宗御製詩贈之，又許世居以寶刀，且曰：「非公不可當此。」

translations.literal: Li Shining practiced occult arts and moved among the nobility; he had once visited Zhao Shiju's mother Kang and presented her with a poem composed by Emperor Renzong, and also promised Shiju a treasured sword, saying: "No one but you is fit to receive this."
translations.idiomatic: Li Shining was a man who trafficked in esoteric arts among the great families; he had once called on Zhao Shiju's mother, Lady Kang, and given her a poem in Emperor Renzong's own hand, and he also promised Shiju a precious sword, saying, "No one but you is worthy to bear this."

sentences.zh: 世居與其黨皆神之，曰：「士寧，二三百歲人也。」

translations.literal: Shiju and his followers all regarded him as divine and said: "Shining is a man of two or three hundred years."
translations.idiomatic: Shiju and his circle treated him as a supernatural being and declared, "Shining is two or three centuries old."

sentences.zh: 解釋其詩，以為至寶之祥。

translations.literal: They interpreted his poem as an omen of supreme treasure.
translations.idiomatic: They read his poem as a sign of an incomparable treasure to come.

sentences.zh: 及鞫世居得之，逮捕士寧，而宰相王安石故與士寧善，百祿劾士寧以妖妄惑世居，致不軌。

translations.literal: When Shiju was interrogated and evidence obtained, Shining was arrested; the chief councilor Wang Anshi had been on good terms with Shining, and Bailu impeached Shining for using sorcery and falsehood to delude Shiju and lead him to treason.
translations.idiomatic: Once the interrogation of Shiju produced evidence, Shining was arrested; Chief Councilor Wang Anshi had long been friendly with Shining, while Bailu charged that Shining had used occult fraud to bewitch Shiju and drive him toward sedition.

sentences.zh: 禧奏：「士寧遺康詩實仁宗製，今獄官以為反，臣不敢同。」

translations.literal: Xi memorialized: "The poem Shining gave Kang was truly composed by Emperor Renzong; now the prison officials treat it as treason—I dare not agree."
translations.idiomatic: Xi submitted a memorial: "The poem Shining gave Lady Kang was genuinely from Emperor Renzong's hand; the investigators now call it treasonous, and I cannot concur."

sentences.zh: 百祿言：「士寧有可死之狀，禧故出之以媚大臣。」

translations.literal: Bailu said: "Shining has grounds for execution; Xi deliberately exonerates him to curry favor with the great minister."
translations.idiomatic: Bailu retorted, "Shining deserves death; Xi is excusing him only to flatter the chief minister."

sentences.zh: 朝廷以御史雜知、樞密承旨參治，而百祿坐報上不實貶，進禧集賢校理、檢正禮房。

translations.literal: The court had the censorate deputy and a privy council delegate join the trial; Bailu was demoted for reporting falsely to the throne, and Xi was advanced to collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies and rectifier of the rites office.
translations.idiomatic: The court added a deputy censor and a privy council delegate to the panel; Bailu was demoted for misreporting to the throne, while Xi was promoted to collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies and rectifier of the rites section.

sentences.zh: 安石與惠卿交惡，鄧綰言惠卿昔居父喪，嘗貸華亭富人錢五百萬買田事，詔禧參鞫。

translations.literal: When Anshi and Huiqing fell out, Deng Wan reported that during his father's mourning Huiqing had once borrowed five million cash from a wealthy man of Huating to buy land; the emperor ordered Xi to assist in the investigation.
translations.idiomatic: After Anshi and Huiqing became estranged, Deng Wan accused Huiqing of having borrowed five million cash from a rich man in Huating to buy land while still in mourning for his father; the emperor instructed Xi to take part in the inquiry.

sentences.zh: 禧陰右惠卿，綰劾之，會綰貶官，獄亦解。

translations.literal: Xi secretly supported Huiqing; Wan impeached him, but Wan was soon demoted and the case was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Xi quietly sided with Huiqing; Wan impeached him for it, yet Wan was soon demoted himself and the case collapsed.

sentences.zh: 禧出為荊湖北路轉運副使。

translations.literal: Xi was sent out as deputy transport commissioner of Jinghu North Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Xi was posted as deputy transport commissioner on the Jinghu North circuit.

sentences.zh: 元豐初，召知諫院。

translations.literal: Early in the Yuanfeng reign he was summoned to direct the Remonstrance Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Yuanfeng era he was recalled to head the Remonstrance Bureau.

sentences.zh: 惠卿在鄜延，欲更蕃漢兵戰守條約，諸老將不謂然，帝頗采聽，將推其法於他路，遣禧往經畫。

translations.literal: Huiqing was at Fuyan and wished to revise the treaties on war and defense for tribal and Han troops; veteran generals disagreed, yet the emperor largely listened to him and planned to extend his system to other circuits, sending Xi to plan it.
translations.idiomatic: While serving on the Fuyan frontier, Huiqing wanted to overhaul the regulations governing tribal and Han forces in attack and defense; the old generals objected, but the emperor largely accepted his views and intended to extend the scheme to other circuits, dispatching Xi to lay out the details.

sentences.zh: 禧是惠卿議，渭帥蔡延慶亦以為不然，帝召延慶還，加禧直龍圖閣，使往代，以母憂不行。

translations.literal: Xi sided with Huiqing's plan; the Wei circuit commander Cai Yanqing also thought it unwise; the emperor recalled Yanqing and gave Xi direct appointment to the Dragon Diagram Hall, sending him to replace him, but he did not go because of his mother's death.
translations.idiomatic: Xi endorsed Huiqing's proposal; Cai Yanqing, commander on the Wei frontier, disagreed as well; the emperor recalled Yanqing, granted Xi direct appointment to the Dragon Diagram Hall, and ordered him to take Yanqing's place, but mourning for his mother kept him from going.

sentences.zh: 服除，召試知制誥兼御史中丞。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was summoned and examined for drafting imperial edicts concurrently with the post of censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: After the mourning period he was called back, examined, and appointed drafter of imperial edicts while also serving as censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 官制行，罷知制誥，專為中丞。

translations.literal: When the new official system took effect the edict-drafting post was abolished and he served solely as censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: After the bureaucratic reform took effect he relinquished the edict-drafting role and held only the censor-in-chiefship.

sentences.zh: 鄧綰守長安，禧疏其過，帝知其以惠卿故，雖改綰青州，亦左遷禧給事中。

translations.literal: Deng Wan was defending Chang'an; Xi memorialized his faults; the emperor knew it was because of Huiqing, and though Wan was transferred to Qingzhou, Xi was also demoted to gentleman attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Wan was stationed at Chang'an when Xi impeached him for misconduct; the emperor saw that the move stemmed from the feud with Huiqing, and although Wan was reassigned to Qingzhou, Xi was demoted to gentleman attendant as well.

sentences.zh: 种諤西討，得銀、夏、宥三州而不能守。

translations.literal: Zhong E campaigned westward and took the three prefectures of Yin, Xia, and You but could not hold them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong E led the western campaign and captured Yin, Xia, and You prefectures, yet proved unable to keep them.

sentences.zh: 延帥沈括欲盡城橫山，瞰平夏，城永樂，詔禧與內侍李舜舉往相其事，令括總兵以從，李稷主饋餉。

translations.literal: The Yan circuit commander Shen Kuo wished to fortify the entire Hengshan line to overlook Pingxia and build Yongle City; the emperor ordered Xi and the inner attendant Li Shunju to go survey the project, with Kuo commanding the army to follow and Li Ji in charge of supplies.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Kuo, commander on the Yan frontier, wanted to ring Hengshan with fortresses overlooking Pingxia and to build Yongle City; the court sent Xi and the eunuch Li Shunju to inspect the site, with Kuo commanding the troops and Li Ji overseeing logistics.

sentences.zh: 禧言：「銀州雖據明堂川、無定河之會，而故城東南已為河水所吞，其西北又阻天塹，實不如永樂之形勢險厄。

translations.literal: Xi said: "Although Yin Prefecture sits at the junction of Mingtang River and the Wuding, the southeast of the old city has already been swallowed by the river and the northwest is blocked by a natural barrier—it is truly inferior to Yongle's steep and narrow terrain.
translations.idiomatic: Xi argued, "Yin Prefecture may stand where the Mingtang and Wuding rivers meet, but the southeastern quarter of the old city has been eaten away by the water and the northwest is cut off by a natural chasm; in truth its ground is far less defensible than Yongle's rugged position.

sentences.zh: 竊惟銀、夏、宥三州，陷沒百年，一日興復，於邊將事功，實為俊偉，軍鋒士氣，固已百倍；

translations.literal: I consider that Yin, Xia, and You, lost for a century, were recovered in a single day—a splendid achievement for frontier generals—and army spirit is already a hundredfold;
translations.idiomatic: I would note that Yin, Xia, and You had lain in enemy hands for a hundred years and were restored in a day—a magnificent feat for any frontier commander—and troop morale is already many times what it was;

sentences.zh: 但建州之始，煩費不貲。

translations.literal: but at the outset of establishing prefectures the expense is beyond reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: yet founding new prefectures at the start entails costs beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 若選擇要會，建置堡柵，名雖非州，實有其地，舊來疆塞，乃在腹心。

translations.literal: If we choose strategic points and build forts and stockades, though not called prefectures they would hold real territory, and the old frontier defenses would lie deep within our core.
translations.idiomatic: If we select key positions and erect forts and palisades, they need not be called prefectures to control real ground, and what were once outer defenses would sit well inside our heartland.

sentences.zh: 已與沈括議築砦堡各六。

translations.literal: I have already discussed with Shen Kuo building six stockades and six forts each.
translations.idiomatic: Kuo and I have already agreed to build six stockades and six forts apiece.

sentences.zh: 砦之大者周九百步，小者五百步，堡之大者二百步，小者百步，用工二十三萬。」

translations.literal: The largest stockade would measure nine hundred paces in circumference, the smallest five hundred; the largest fort two hundred paces, the smallest one hundred; labor would require two hundred thirty thousand man-days."
translations.idiomatic: The largest stockade would ring nine hundred paces, the smallest five hundred; the largest fort two hundred paces, the smallest one hundred; the project would demand two hundred thirty thousand man-days of labor."

sentences.zh: 遂城永樂，十四日而成。

translations.literal: They then walled Yongle, completing it in fourteen days.
translations.idiomatic: They went ahead and walled Yongle, finishing the work in fourteen days.

sentences.zh: 禧、括、舜舉還米脂。

translations.literal: Xi, Kuo, and Shunju returned to Mizhi.
translations.idiomatic: Xi, Kuo, and Shunju withdrew to Mizhi.

sentences.zh: 明日，夏兵數千騎趨新城，禧亟往視之。

translations.literal: The next day several thousand Xia horsemen advanced on the new city; Xi hurried to inspect it.
translations.idiomatic: The following day several thousand Xia cavalry rode toward the new fortress, and Xi rushed to see for himself.

sentences.zh: 或說禧曰：「初被詔相城，禦寇，非職也。」

translations.literal: Someone advised Xi: "You were first ordered to survey the city site; repelling the enemy is not your duty."
translations.idiomatic: Someone urged Xi, "Your original commission was only to choose the site; fighting off the enemy was never part of your brief."

sentences.zh: 禧不聽，與舜舉、稷俱行，括獨守米脂。

translations.literal: Xi would not listen and went with Shunju and Ji, while Kuo alone held Mizhi.
translations.idiomatic: Xi refused to heed him and set out with Shunju and Ji, leaving Kuo alone at Mizhi.

sentences.zh: 先是，种諤還自京師，極言城永樂非計，禧怒變色，謂諤曰：「君獨不畏死乎？

translations.literal: Earlier, when Zhong E returned from the capital and strongly argued that fortifying Yongle was a mistake, Xi flushed with anger and said to him: "Are you alone unafraid of death?
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Zhong E came back from the capital and insisted that building Yongle was folly, Xi turned crimson and demanded, "Are you the only man here who does not fear death?

sentences.zh: 敢誤成事。」

translations.literal: You dare obstruct the accomplishment of the task."
translations.idiomatic: How dare you obstruct what we are trying to accomplish?"

sentences.zh: 諤曰：「城之必敗，敗則死，拒節制亦死；

translations.literal: E said: "If we build it we are sure to fail; if we fail we die, and if we defy command we also die;
translations.idiomatic: E replied, "If we build it the position is doomed; when it falls we die, and if we disobey orders we die as well;

sentences.zh: 死於此，猶愈於喪國師而淪異域也。」

translations.literal: to die here is still better than losing the state's army and falling into alien lands."
translations.idiomatic: dying here is still preferable to losing the imperial army and being overrun on foreign soil."

sentences.zh: 禧度不可屈，奏諤跋扈異議，詔諤守延州。

translations.literal: Seeing he could not bend him, Xi memorialized that E was insubordinate and dissenting; the emperor ordered E to defend Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Convinced that E would not yield, Xi reported him for insubordination and obstruction; the court ordered E to hold Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 夏兵二十萬屯涇原北，聞城永樂，即來爭邊。

translations.literal: Two hundred thousand Xia troops camped north of Jingyuan; hearing that Yongle was being walled, they came at once to contest the border.
translations.idiomatic: Two hundred thousand Xia soldiers massed north of Jingyuan; as soon as they learned Yongle was being fortified, they marched to dispute the frontier.

sentences.zh: 人馳告者十數，禧等皆不之信，曰：「彼若大來，是吾立功取富貴之秋也。」

translations.literal: A dozen messengers rode in with reports, yet Xi and the others refused to believe them, saying: "If they come in force, this is our season to win merit and seize wealth and rank."
translations.idiomatic: A dozen couriers galloped in with warnings, but Xi and his party dismissed them, saying, "If the enemy comes in strength, this is our chance to win glory and fortune."

sentences.zh: 禧亟赴之，大將高永亨曰：「城小人寡，又無水，不可守。」

translations.literal: Xi hurried thither; the general Gao Yongheng said: "The city is small, the men few, and there is no water—it cannot be held."
translations.idiomatic: Xi pressed on at once; the general Gao Yongheng warned, "The fortress is small, the garrison thin, and there is no water—we cannot hold it."

sentences.zh: 禧以為沮眾，欲斬之，既而械送延獄。

translations.literal: Xi regarded this as discouraging the troops and wished to execute him, but instead had him shackled and sent to the Yan circuit prison.
translations.idiomatic: Xi took this for demoralizing the men and meant to behead him, but in the end had him bound and sent to the Yan circuit jail.

sentences.zh: 比至，夏兵傾國而至，永亨兄永能請及其未陳擊之，禧曰：「爾何知，王師不鼓不成列。」

translations.literal: By the time they arrived the Xia had mobilized the whole realm; Yongheng's elder brother Yongneng asked to strike before they formed ranks, but Xi said: "What do you know? The imperial army does not advance until the drums have beaten and the ranks are formed."
translations.idiomatic: When they arrived the Xia had thrown their entire strength into the field; Yongheng's elder brother Yongneng urged an attack before the enemy could deploy, but Xi snapped, "What do you know of such things? Imperial troops do not strike until the drums have sounded and the ranks are set."

sentences.zh: 禧執刀自率士卒拒戰。

translations.literal: Xi took a blade in hand and personally led the soldiers to resist.
translations.idiomatic: Gripping his sword, Xi personally led the men into battle.

sentences.zh: 夏人益眾，分陣迭攻抵城下。

translations.literal: The Xia grew ever more numerous, dividing into formations and attacking in waves until they reached the foot of the wall.
translations.idiomatic: More and more Xia poured in, splitting into columns and assaulting in relays until they were under the walls.

sentences.zh: 曲珍兵陳於水際，官軍不利，將士皆有懼色。

translations.literal: Qu Zhen drew up his troops along the water's edge; the government army fared poorly and officers and men alike showed fear.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Zhen formed his line along the riverbank; the imperial forces were getting the worse of it, and officers and soldiers alike looked frightened.

sentences.zh: 珍白禧曰：「今眾心已搖，不可戰，戰必敗，請收兵入城。」

translations.literal: Zhen reported to Xi: "Morale is already shaken; we must not fight—if we fight we are sure to lose. Please withdraw the troops into the city."
translations.idiomatic: Zhen told Xi, "The men's hearts are already wavering; we cannot fight—if we do we are doomed. Pull the army back inside the walls."

sentences.zh: 禧曰：「君為大將，奈何遇敵不戰，先自退邪？」

translations.literal: Xi said: "You are a senior commander—how can you meet the enemy and refuse to fight, retreating of your own accord?"
translations.idiomatic: Xi shot back, "You are a senior commander—how can you face the enemy and refuse to fight, running before anyone else?"

sentences.zh: 俄夏騎卒度水犯陳。

translations.literal: Soon Xia horsemen crossed the water and struck the formation.
translations.idiomatic: In moments Xia cavalry forded the stream and crashed into the line.

sentences.zh: 鄜延選鋒軍最為驍銳，皆一當百，銀槍錦襖，光彩耀日，先接戰而敗，奔入城，蹂後陳。

translations.literal: The Fuyan picked vanguard was the fiercest, each man a match for a hundred, with silver spears and brocade coats dazzling in the sun; they engaged first and were defeated, fleeing into the city and trampling the rear ranks.
translations.idiomatic: The Fuyan picked vanguard—men who counted as a hundred each, in silver spears and brocade coats that blazed in the sunlight—met the enemy first, broke, and bolted for the gate, crushing the units behind them.

sentences.zh: 夏人乘之，師大潰，死及棄甲南奔者幾半。

translations.literal: The Xia pressed the advantage; the army collapsed in great disorder, and nearly half were killed or cast off their armor and fled south.
translations.idiomatic: The Xia pressed the rout; the army shattered, and nearly half the men were killed or threw away their armor and fled south.

sentences.zh: 珍與殘兵入城，崖峻徑窄，騎卒緣崖而上，喪馬八千匹，遂受圍。

translations.literal: Zhen and the survivors entered the city; the cliffs were steep and the paths narrow, and horsemen had to climb the cliff face—eight thousand horses were lost—and they were besieged.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen and the remnants scrambled into the fortress; the cliffs were sheer and the paths tight, and horsemen had to lead their mounts up the rock face—eight thousand horses were lost—and the garrison was surrounded.

sentences.zh: 水砦為夏人所據，掘井不及泉，士卒渴死者太半。

translations.literal: The water fort was seized by the Xia; wells were dug but did not reach water, and more than half the soldiers died of thirst.
translations.idiomatic: The Xia took the water bastion; wells were sunk but never struck water, and more than half the troops died of thirst.

sentences.zh: 夏人蟻附登城，尚扶創拒鬥。

translations.literal: The Xia swarmed up the wall like ants; the defenders still fought on despite their wounds.
translations.idiomatic: The Xia swarmed the walls like ants; the defenders still fought on, propping up their wounded.

sentences.zh: 珍度不可敵，又白禧，請突圍而南；

translations.literal: Zhen judged the enemy could not be withstood and again reported to Xi, asking to break out to the south;
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the enemy could not be beaten, Zhen again appealed to Xi to break out toward the south;

sentences.zh: 永能亦勸李稷盡捐金帛，募死士力戰以出，皆不聽。

translations.literal: Yongneng also urged Li Ji to cast all gold and silk to recruit daredevils for a desperate fight to escape, but none of this was heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Yongneng likewise urged Li Ji to pour out all the gold and silk, hire daredevils, and fight their way out, but Xi would hear none of it.

sentences.zh: 戊戌夜大雨，城陷，四將走免，禧、舜舉、稷死之，永能沒於陳。

translations.literal: On the night of the wuxu day a great rain fell and the city fell; four generals escaped, while Xi, Shunju, and Ji died, and Yongneng perished in battle.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuxu night a torrential rain fell and the city was lost; four generals got away, but Xi, Shunju, and Ji were killed, and Yongneng died in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 初，括奏夏兵來逼城，見官兵整，故還。

translations.literal: Earlier Kuo had reported that Xia troops came to threaten the city but withdrew on seeing the government army in good order.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Kuo had reported that Xia forces approached the fortress but withdrew when they saw the imperial troops in good order.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「括料敵疏矣，彼來未出戰，豈肯遽退邪？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Kuo's reading of the enemy is shallow; they came without fighting—how could they withdraw so quickly?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Kuo's estimate of the enemy is naive; they came without giving battle—why would they pull back so soon?

sentences.zh: 必有大兵在後。」

translations.literal: There must be a great army behind them."
translations.idiomatic: A large force must be following behind."

sentences.zh: 已而果然。

translations.literal: And so it proved.
translations.idiomatic: Events soon proved him right.

sentences.zh: 帝聞禧等死，涕泣悲憤，為之不食。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard that Xi and the others had died, he wept in grief and anger and would not eat because of it.
translations.idiomatic: When word came that Xi and the others had perished, the emperor wept in grief and rage and refused food for days.

sentences.zh: 贈禧金紫光祿大夫、吏部尚書，諡曰「忠湣」。

translations.literal: Xi was posthumously given the titles of Grandee of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Minister of Personnel, with the posthumous name "Loyal and Grieving."
translations.idiomatic: Xi was posthumously ennobled as Grandee of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Minister of Personnel, with the posthumous epithet "Loyal and Grieving."

sentences.zh: 官其家二十人。

translations.literal: Twenty members of his family were given office.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty members of his household were granted official posts.

sentences.zh: 稷工部侍郎，官其家十二人。

translations.literal: Ji was made vice minister of works and twelve in his family were given office.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was posthumously made vice minister of works, and twelve members of his family received appointments.

sentences.zh: 禧疏曠有膽略，好談兵，每云西北可唾手取，恨將帥怯爾。

translations.literal: Xi was open and bold, fond of discussing warfare, and often said the northwest could be taken at a wave of the hand, blaming only the timidity of generals.
translations.idiomatic: Xi was expansive and fearless, loved to talk of war, and often declared that the northwest could be seized with a flick of the wrist, blaming nothing but the cowardice of the commanders.

sentences.zh: 呂惠卿力引之，故不次用。

translations.literal: Lü Huiqing strongly recommended him, and so he was employed out of regular order.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Huiqing pushed him hard, which is why he rose by irregular promotion.

sentences.zh: 自靈武之敗，秦、晉困棘，天下企望息兵，而沈括、种諤陳進取之策。

translations.literal: Since the defeat at Lingwu, Qin and Jin were in dire straits and the realm longed for peace, yet Shen Kuo and Zhong E urged policies of advance.
translations.idiomatic: After the disaster at Lingwu, the Qin and Jin regions were in distress and the empire yearned for peace, yet Shen Kuo and Zhong E pressed plans for further conquest.

sentences.zh: 禧素以邊事自任，狂謀輕敵，猝與強虜遇，至於覆沒。

translations.literal: Xi had always taken frontier affairs upon himself; with reckless plans and contempt for the enemy he suddenly met a powerful foe and was destroyed to the last man.
translations.idiomatic: Xi had long styled himself master of frontier affairs; his rash schemes and contempt for the enemy brought him suddenly against a formidable foe, and his force was wiped out.

sentences.zh: 自是之後，帝始知邊臣不可信倚，深自悔咎，遂不復用兵，無意於西伐矣。

translations.literal: From this time the emperor came to know that frontier officials could not be trusted and deeply reproached himself; he then ceased to use the army and had no mind for western campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: From that point the emperor realized frontier officers could not be relied upon, blamed himself bitterly, and never again took up arms with any thought of campaigning west.

sentences.zh: 子：俯，自有傳。

translations.literal: Son: Fu, who has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fu has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 李稷

translations.literal: Li Ji
translations.idiomatic: Li Ji

translations.literal: (Appended biography)
translations.idiomatic: (Appended biography)

sentences.zh: 李稷，字長卿，邛州人。

translations.literal: Li Ji, style name Changqing, was a man of Qiong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ji, whose style name was Changqing, came from Qiong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父絢，龍圖閣直學士。

translations.literal: His father Xuan was a direct academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xuan had been a direct academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall.

sentences.zh: 稷用蔭歷管庫，權河北西路轉運判官，修拓深、趙、邢三州城，役無愆素，然峭刻嚴忍。

translations.literal: Ji entered service by yin privilege and passed through storehouse posts; as acting transport judge of Hebei West Circuit he expanded the walls of Shen, Zhao, and Xing prefectures without delay or waste in the labor, yet he was harsh, exacting, and cruel.
translations.idiomatic: Ji entered government by hereditary privilege and worked his way through fiscal posts; as acting transport judge on the Hebei West circuit he enlarged the walls of Shen, Zhao, and Xing without waste or delay in the corvée, yet he was severe, exacting, and pitiless.

sentences.zh: 察訪使者以為言，都水丞程昉亦訴其越職。

translations.literal: Inspection envoys reported on this, and the director of waterways Cheng Fang also accused him of overstepping his duties.
translations.idiomatic: Inspection commissioners complained of his methods, and Cheng Fang, director of waterways, also charged him with exceeding his authority.

sentences.zh: 詔令件析。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the charges itemized and analyzed.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered each charge set out and examined.

sentences.zh: 御史周尹又論稷父死二十年不葬，僅徙東路，俄提舉蜀部茶場。

translations.literal: Censor Zhou Yin also charged that twenty years after his father's death Ji had still not buried him; he was merely transferred to the eastern route, and soon after was made supervisor of the Shu tea monopoly.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Zhou Yin further accused Ji of leaving his father unburied for twenty years; he was only shifted to the eastern route, and shortly afterward was put in charge of the Shu tea monopoly.

sentences.zh: 甫兩歲，羨課七十六萬緡，擢鹽鐵判官。

translations.literal: In barely two years he produced a surplus revenue of seven hundred sixty thousand strings of cash and was promoted to salt and iron commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In scarcely two years he turned a surplus of seven hundred sixty thousand strings of cash and was promoted to salt and iron commissioner.

sentences.zh: 詔推揚其功以勸在位，遂為陝西轉運使、制置解鹽。

translations.literal: An edict publicized his achievement to encourage those in office, and he became Shaanxi transport commissioner and commissioner for arranging Jie salt.
translations.idiomatic: The court publicized his achievement to spur others in office, and he was made Shaanxi transport commissioner with charge over the Jie salt monopoly.

sentences.zh: 秦民作舍道傍者，創使納「侵街錢」，一路擾怨，與李察皆以苛暴著稱。

translations.literal: For Qin people who built houses beside the road he newly required payment of "street-encroachment money," stirring resentment along the whole route; he and Li Cha were both notorious for harsh cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: He invented a levy called "street-encroachment money" on Qin peasants who built along the highways, provoking resentment across the circuit; he and Li Cha were both infamous for brutal exactions.

sentences.zh: 時人語曰：「寧逢黑殺，莫逢稷、察」。

translations.literal: People of the time said: "Better to meet the Black Killer than to meet Ji and Cha."
translations.idiomatic: A saying of the day ran, "Better to run into the Black Killer than into Ji and Cha."

sentences.zh: 种諤起興、靈議，稷聞之亦上言：「可令邊面諸將各出兵撓之，使不得耕種，則其國必困，國困眾離，取可決也。」

translations.literal: When Zhong E raised the plan to recover Xing and Ling, Ji heard of it and also memorialized: "The frontier commanders can each send troops to harass them so they cannot plant or harvest; their state will surely be distressed, and when the state is distressed the people scatter—then conquest is assured."
translations.idiomatic: When Zhong E revived the proposal to recover Xing and Ling, Ji heard of it and submitted his own plan: "Let every frontier commander send out raiding parties so the enemy cannot sow or reap; their state will grow desperate, and when it is desperate and the people scatter, victory is certain."

sentences.zh: 及出境，稷督餉，民苦折運，多散逸，稷令騎士執之，斷其足筋，宛轉山谷間，凡數十人，累日乃得死。

translations.literal: Once the army crossed the border Ji supervised supplies; the people suffered from relay transport and many fled; Ji ordered horsemen to seize them, sever their heel tendons, and leave them writhing in the valleys—several dozen men who took many days to die.
translations.idiomatic: Once the campaign crossed the border Ji oversaw logistics; civilians groaned under relay transport and many deserted; Ji had horsemen seize them, sever their heel tendons, and leave them writhing in the ravines—several dozen men who took days to die.

sentences.zh: 始，稷受旨得斬郡守以下，於是上下相臨以峻法，雖小吏護丁夫，亦顓戮不請。

translations.literal: At the outset Ji had received orders empowering him to execute anyone down to prefects; thus superiors and subordinates enforced one another with severe law, and even petty clerks overseeing corvée laborers would kill on their own authority without asking leave.
translations.idiomatic: From the start Ji had been authorized to execute anyone as low as a prefect; the whole chain of command now policed itself with draconian penalties, and even minor clerks overseeing corvée gangs would kill men outright without seeking permission.

sentences.zh: 軍食竟不繼，諤謀斬稷，客呂大鈞引義責之，復使還取糧。

translations.literal: Army provisions in the end did not keep up; E planned to execute Ji, but his guest Lü Dajun rebuked him on principle of righteousness and had him sent back to fetch grain.
translations.idiomatic: Supplies never kept pace with the army; E meant to execute Ji, but his adviser Lü Dajun appealed to duty and righteousness and persuaded him to send Ji back for more grain.

sentences.zh: 既集，諤猶宣言稷乏軍興，致大功不就，坐削兩秩，貶為判官。

translations.literal: After supplies were gathered E still declared that Ji's failure in military provisioning had prevented the great achievement from being accomplished; Ji was demoted two ranks and reduced to judge.
translations.idiomatic: Even after the grain arrived, E still proclaimed that Ji's failure to provision the campaign had ruined the great enterprise; Ji was stripped of two ranks and demoted to judge.

sentences.zh: 永樂既城，稷悉輦金、銀、鈔、帛充牣其中，欲誇示徐禧，以為城甫就而中已實。

translations.literal: Once Yongle was walled, Ji had all gold, silver, notes, and silk carted in to fill it, wishing to display this to Xu Xi and show that though the city was just finished its interior was already stocked full.
translations.idiomatic: After Yongle was walled, Ji had gold, silver, paper notes, and silk hauled in until the storehouses overflowed, eager to impress Xu Xi with the claim that the fortress was barely finished yet already fully provisioned.

sentences.zh: 積金既多，故受圍愈急，而稷守之不敢去，以及於難。

translations.literal: Because so much treasure had been accumulated, the siege grew all the fiercer, yet Ji guarded it and dared not leave, and so met disaster.
translations.idiomatic: The hoard of treasure made the Xia press the siege all the harder, yet Ji clung to it and would not abandon the city, and so perished with it.

sentences.zh: 李舜舉別有傳。

translations.literal: Li Shunju has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shunju has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 高永能

translations.literal: Gao Yongneng
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yongneng

sentences.zh: 高永能，字君舉，世為綏州人。

translations.literal: Gao Yongneng, style name Junju, was for generations a man of Sui Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yongneng, whose style name was Junju, came from a Sui Prefecture family of many generations.

sentences.zh: 初，伯祖文岯舉州來歸，即拜團練使，已而棄之北遷，其祖文玉獨留居延川，至永能始家青澗。

translations.literal: At first his great-uncle Wen Yan had surrendered the whole prefecture and was at once made militia training commissioner, but later abandoned it and moved north; his grandfather Wen Yu alone remained at Yanchuan, and it was with Yongneng that the family first settled at Qingjian.
translations.idiomatic: His great-uncle Wen Yan had once surrendered Sui Prefecture and was immediately made militia training commissioner, but later abandoned the post and moved north; his grandfather Wen Yu alone stayed behind at Yanchuan, and the family first established itself at Qingjian in Yongneng's generation.

sentences.zh: 少有勇力，善騎射，由行伍補殿侍，稍遷供奉官。

translations.literal: In youth he had courage and strength and was skilled in mounted archery; from the ranks he was appointed palace attendant and gradually promoted to tribute bearer.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he was strong and brave and excelled at mounted archery; rising from the ranks he became a palace attendant and was gradually promoted to tribute bearer.

sentences.zh: 种諤取綏州，發永能兵六千先驅入囉兀，五戰皆捷，轉供備庫副使。

translations.literal: When Zhong E took Sui Prefecture he sent Yongneng with six thousand men as vanguard into Luowu; in five battles all were victorious, and he was transferred to deputy commissioner of the supply reserve depot.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhong E captured Sui Prefecture he dispatched Yongneng with six thousand troops as vanguard into Luowu; after five victories in succession he was made deputy commissioner of the supply reserve depot.

sentences.zh: 治綏德城，辟地四千頃，增戶千三百，即知城事。

translations.literal: He administered Suide City, opened four thousand qing of land, added thirteen hundred households, and was then made administrator of the city.
translations.idiomatic: He developed Suide City, reclaimed four thousand qing of land, added thirteen hundred households, and was put in charge of the city administration.

sentences.zh: 元豐初，為鄜延都監。

translations.literal: Early in the Yuanfeng reign he became Fuyan circuit supervisory commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Yuanfeng era he was made supervisory commissioner on the Fuyan circuit.

sentences.zh: 秋，大稔，夏人屯二千騎於大會平，將取稼。

translations.literal: In autumn the harvest was abundant; the Xia stationed two thousand horsemen at Dahui Ping intending to seize the grain.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn brought a bumper harvest; the Xia posted two thousand horsemen at Dahui Ping to raid the crops.

sentences.zh: 永能簡精騎突過其營，騎卒驚潰，獲鈐轄二人。

translations.literal: Yongneng chose elite horsemen to charge through their camp; the riders panicked and fled, and two deputy commissioners were captured.
translations.idiomatic: Yongneng led picked cavalry in a sudden strike through their camp; the enemy horsemen broke in panic, and two deputy commissioners were taken.

sentences.zh: 轉六宅使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to commissioner of the Six Mansions.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to commissioner of the Six Mansions.

sentences.zh: 夏人患之，令曰：「有得高六宅者，賞金等其身。」

translations.literal: The Xia were troubled by him and issued an order: "Whoever captures Gao of the Six Mansions will be rewarded with gold equal to his weight."
translations.idiomatic: The Xia came to fear him and proclaimed, "Whoever captures Gao of the Six Mansions shall receive gold equal to his body weight."

sentences.zh: 經略使呂惠卿行邊，永能伏騎谷中，以備侵軼，邊騎果至，馳出擊走之。

translations.literal: When frontier commissioner Lü Huiqing toured the border, Yongneng hid horsemen in a ravine to guard against raids; frontier riders indeed came and he galloped out and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: When frontier commissioner Lü Huiqing inspected the border, Yongneng concealed cavalry in a gorge against incursions; enemy scouts appeared as expected, and he charged out and routed them.

sentences.zh: 夏兵二萬犯當川堡，永能以千騎與相遇，度不能支，依險設疑兵，且鬥且卻，而令後騎揚塵，若援兵至者，奮而前，遂解去。

translations.literal: Twenty thousand Xia troops attacked Dangchuan Fort; Yongneng met them with a thousand horsemen, judged he could not hold, used the terrain to set up a decoy force, fought while retreating, and had rear riders raise dust as if reinforcements had arrived, then charged forward and the enemy withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When twenty thousand Xia attacked Dangchuan Fort, Yongneng met them with a thousand cavalry; seeing he could not prevail, he used the terrain to feign reinforcements, fought a fighting retreat while rear elements raised dust as though aid had come, then surged forward and the enemy withdrew.

sentences.zh: 擢本路鈐轄。

translations.literal: He was promoted to circuit deputy commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was elevated to deputy commissioner of the circuit.

sentences.zh: 四年，西討，永能為前鋒，圍米脂城。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of the western campaign Yongneng served as vanguard and besieged Mizhi City.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of the western expedition he served as vanguard and besieged Mizhi.

sentences.zh: 邊人十萬來援，永能謂弟永亨曰：「彼恃眾集易吾軍，營當大川，宜嚴陳待其至，張左右翼擊之，可破也。」

translations.literal: A hundred thousand border people came to relieve it; Yongneng told his younger brother Yongheng: "They rely on their massed numbers to overwhelm us; camp on the great river and wait in strict formation for their arrival, then strike with left and right wings and they can be broken."
translations.idiomatic: A hundred thousand tribal allies came to the relief; Yongneng told his brother Yongheng, "They trust their numbers to crush us; encamp on the broad river, hold a tight formation until they arrive, then hit them with both wings and they will break."

sentences.zh: 詰旦，鏖戰於無定河，斬首數千級，得馬三千、橐駝牛羊萬計。

translations.literal: At dawn they fought fiercely on the Wuding River, beheading several thousand, and took three thousand horses and tens of thousands of camels, cattle, and sheep.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn they fought a bitter battle on the Wuding River, taking several thousand heads, three thousand horses, and tens of thousands of camels, cattle, and sheep.

sentences.zh: 城猶未下，密遣諜說降其東壁守將，衣以文錦，導以鼓吹，耀諸城下，酋令介訛遇乃出降。

translations.literal: The city had not yet fallen; he secretly sent agents to persuade the eastern-wall commander to surrender, clothed him in brocade, led him with drums and pipes, and displayed him below the walls; the chieftain Lingjie Eyu then came out and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: The city still held out; he sent secret agents to win over the eastern-wall commander, dressed him in brocade, paraded him with drums and pipes beneath the walls, and the chieftain Lingjie Eyu then surrendered.

sentences.zh: 進東上閤門使、寧州刺史，以年請老，不許，又進四方館使、榮州團練使。

translations.literal: He was advanced to eastern upper gate envoy and prefect of Ningzhou; he requested retirement on grounds of age but was refused, and was further made envoy of the Four Directions Hall and militia training commissioner of Rongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to eastern upper gate envoy and prefect of Ningzhou; pleading age he asked to retire but was denied, and was further made envoy of the Four Directions Hall and militia training commissioner of Rongzhou.

sentences.zh: 永樂之役，獻謀皆不用。

translations.literal: In the Yongle campaign his plans were all rejected.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongle disaster every plan he offered was ignored.

sentences.zh: 城既陷，其孫昌裔欲援之從間道出，永能歎曰：「吾結髮從事西羌，戰未嚐挫，今年已七十，受國大恩，恨無以報，此吾死所也。」

translations.literal: After the city fell his grandson Changyi wished to rescue him by a hidden route; Yongneng sighed and said: "I have served the western Qiang since youth and never met defeat in battle; this year I am seventy and have received great grace from the state—I regret I cannot repay it; this is where I shall die."
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell his grandson Changyi wanted to reach him by a secret path; Yongneng sighed and said, "I have fought the western tribes since youth and never knew defeat; this year I am seventy, and the state has shown me great favor—I only regret I cannot repay it; this is where I die."

sentences.zh: 顧易一卒敝衣，戰而死。

translations.literal: He exchanged clothes with a common soldier in rags and died fighting.
translations.idiomatic: He swapped clothes with a ragged private and died in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 其子世亮與昌裔求得屍以歸。

translations.literal: His son Shiliang and Changyi recovered the body and brought it home.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shiliang and Changyi recovered the corpse and returned it home.

sentences.zh: 詔贈房州觀察使，錄世亮為忠州刺史，諸孫皆侍禁殿直。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously made him observation commissioner of Fangzhou, enrolled Shiliang as prefect of Zhongzhou, and all his grandsons were made palace attendants and imperial guardsmen.
translations.idiomatic: The court posthumously made him observation commissioner of Fangzhou, appointed Shiliang prefect of Zhongzhou, and enrolled all his grandsons as palace attendants and imperial guardsmen.

sentences.zh: 永能家世州將，所領多故部曲，拊之有恩惠，遇敵則身先之。

translations.literal: Yongneng's family for generations were prefectural commanders; those he led were mostly old retainers; he treated them with kindness and in battle went before them.
translations.idiomatic: The Gaos had been frontier commanders for generations; most of his troops were old retainers whom he treated generously and always led from the front.

sentences.zh: 下有傷者，載以己副馬，故能得士死力。

translations.literal: When subordinates were wounded he carried them on his own spare horse, and so won men to die for him.
translations.idiomatic: When men under him were wounded he gave them his own spare mount, and so won their willingness to die for him.

sentences.zh: 遠近喜言其事，稱之曰「老高」。

translations.literal: People near and far delighted to tell of him and called him "Old Gao."
translations.idiomatic: People throughout the region loved to tell stories of him and called him "Old Gao."

sentences.zh: 及死，邊人無不痛惜。

translations.literal: At his death the border people all grieved.
translations.idiomatic: When he died the frontier people mourned him deeply.

sentences.zh: 嘗過其遠祖唐綏州刺史思祥淘沙川廟，得畫像及神道碑，上之，詔即所在賜田三十頃，以奉祭祀。

translations.literal: He once passed the shrine of his remote ancestor Tang Sui prefectural commander Si Xiang at Taosha River and obtained his portrait and spirit-way stele; he presented them to the throne, and an edict granted thirty qing of fields on the spot for sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Passing the shrine of his distant ancestor, Tang Sui prefect Si Xiang, at Taosha River, he found a portrait and spirit-way stele, presented them to court, and received an edict granting thirty qing of land on the spot for sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 永能之亡，延州將皇城使寇偉亦力戰而沒，贈均州防禦使。

translations.literal: At Yongneng's death Yanzhou commander Kou Wei also fought fiercely and perished; he was posthumously made defense commissioner of Junzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Yongneng fell, Yanzhou commander Kou Wei also fought to the death and was posthumously made defense commissioner of Junzhou.

sentences.zh: 沈起，字興宗，明州鄞人。

translations.literal: Shen Qi, style name Xingzong, was a man of Yin in Ming Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Qi, whose style name was Xingzong, came from Yin in Ming Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 進士高第，調滁州判官，與監真州轉般倉。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination with high standing and was appointed judge of Chuzhou, and supervised the transport granary at Zhenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He took the jinshi with high honors and became judge of Chuzhou, then supervised the transport granary at Zhenzhou.

sentences.zh: 聞父病，委官歸侍，以喪免，有司劾其擅去。

translations.literal: Hearing his father was ill, he left his post to nurse him; after the funeral he was dismissed from office and the authorities impeached him for leaving without permission.
translations.idiomatic: When he learned his father was ill he abandoned his post to care for him; after the funeral he was removed from office and impeached for unauthorized departure.

sentences.zh: 終喪，薦書應格當遷用，帝謂輔臣曰：「觀過知仁。

translations.literal: When mourning ended his recommendation qualified him for promotion; the emperor told his councilors: "By observing faults one knows virtue.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his recommendation qualified him for promotion; the emperor told his ministers, "One knows a man's character by watching his mistakes.

sentences.zh: 今由父疾而致罪，何以厚風教而勸天下之為人子者。」

translations.literal: Now he is punished because of his father's illness—how can we enrich moral teaching and encourage all who are sons under Heaven?"
translations.idiomatic: If we punish him for tending a sick father, how can we strengthen public morals and encourage filial sons everywhere?"

sentences.zh: 乃特遷之，知海門縣。

translations.literal: He was thereupon specially promoted and made magistrate of Haimen County.
translations.idiomatic: He was thereupon given a special promotion and appointed magistrate of Haimen County.

sentences.zh: 縣負海地卑，間歲海潮至，冒民田舍，民徙以避，棄其業。

translations.literal: The county faced the sea on low ground; every few years the tide surged in and flooded houses and fields, and the people moved away to escape, abandoning their livelihoods.
translations.idiomatic: The county lay on low coastal ground; every few years the sea tide flooded homes and fields, and people fled, abandoning their livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 起為築堤百里，引江水灌溉其中，田益辟，民相率以歸，至立祠以報。

translations.literal: Qi built a dike a hundred li long and drew river water to irrigate the land within; fields expanded and the people returned in groups, even erecting a shrine in gratitude.
translations.idiomatic: Qi built a hundred-li dike and channeled river water to irrigate the enclosed land; farmland expanded, people returned in numbers, and they even raised a shrine in thanks.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞包拯舉為監察御史。

translations.literal: Vice censor-in-chief Bao Zheng recommended him as investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Censor-in-Chief Bao Zheng recommended him as investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 吏部格，選吏以贓私絓法，無輕重終身不遷。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Personnel regulations held that selection officials guilty of graft, regardless of severity, were never to be promoted for life.
translations.idiomatic: Personnel regulations barred any selection official tainted by corruption, however lightly, from promotion for life.

sentences.zh: 起論其情可矜者，可限年敘用，遂著為令。

translations.literal: Qi argued that cases where the circumstances merited compassion might be re-employed after a set term, and this was written into law.
translations.idiomatic: Qi argued that cases deserving mercy might be re-employed after a fixed interval, and the rule was codified.

sentences.zh: 立縣令考課法，設河渠司領諸道水政，乞采漢故事，擇卿大夫子弟入宿衛，選賢良文學高第給事宮省，勿專任宦官，宗室袒免親令補外官，復府兵，汰冗卒，書數十上。

translations.literal: He established examination standards for county magistrates, set up a canals office to oversee water policy in all circuits, begged to follow Han precedent in choosing sons of ministers and grandees for palace guard service, select men of talent and literary distinction for palace secretariat posts, not rely solely on eunuchs, require imperial clansmen in mourning dress to take outer posts, restore the fubing militia, and cut redundant soldiers—memorializing dozens of times.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed magistrate evaluation standards, a canals office to direct waterworks in every circuit, Han-style selection of ministers' sons for palace guard duty, talented literati for palace posts, an end to exclusive reliance on eunuchs, outer appointments for imperial clansmen in mourning, restoration of the militia, and cuts to redundant troops—submitting dozens of memorials.

sentences.zh: 以論興國鐵官事不合，出通判越州，改知蘄、楚二州。

translations.literal: Because his views on the Xingguo iron bureau did not accord with policy he was sent out as vice prefect of Yuezhou and then made prefect of Qi and Chu prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: His views on the Xingguo iron bureau offended the court, so he was made vice prefect of Yuezhou and then prefect of Qi and Chu.

sentences.zh: 京東歲饑盜起，除提點刑獄。

translations.literal: In Jingdong a famine year brought bandits; he was made judicial intendant.
translations.idiomatic: When famine in Jingdong bred banditry he was appointed judicial intendant.

sentences.zh: 至，則開首贖法攜其伍，盜內自睽疑，轉相束縛唯恐後。

translations.literal: On arrival he opened a law of leniency for those who turned themselves in with their accomplices; the bandits grew suspicious of one another and bound one another up, each fearing to be last.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he offered leniency to those who surrendered with their gangs; the bandits turned on one another and tied each other up, each afraid of being last.

sentences.zh: 改開封府判官，為湖南轉運使。

translations.literal: He was changed to Kaifeng vice prefect and made Hunan transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He became vice prefect of Kaifeng and then Hunan transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 凡羽毛、筋革、舟楫、竹箭之材，多出所部，取於民無制，吏挾為奸。

translations.literal: Feathers, sinew, leather, boats, and bamboo shafts mostly came from his circuit and were taken from the people without limit while clerks used this to extort.
translations.idiomatic: Feathers, sinew, leather, boats, and bamboo shafts mostly came from his circuit, seized from the people without limit while clerks extorted them.

sentences.zh: 起會其當用，自與商人貿易，所省什六七。

translations.literal: Qi tallied what was needed, traded directly with merchants himself, and saved six or seven tenths of the cost.
translations.idiomatic: Qi calculated actual needs, traded with merchants directly, and saved sixty or seventy percent of the cost.

sentences.zh: 召為三司鹽鐵副使，直舍人院。

translations.literal: He was summoned as salt and iron vice commissioner and entered the Academy drafting office.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as salt and iron vice commissioner and attached to the Academy drafting office.

sentences.zh: 熙寧三年，韓絳使陝西，加起集賢殿修撰、陝西都轉運使。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xining, when Han Jiang went on mission to Shaanxi, Qi was added as collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies and Shaanxi chief transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the third Xining year, when Han Jiang went to Shaanxi, Qi was made collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies and chief Shaanxi transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 慶州軍變，將寇長安，起率兵討平之。

translations.literal: When Qingzhou troops mutinied and were about to threaten Chang'an, Qi led troops and suppressed them.
translations.idiomatic: When Qingzhou mutinied and threatened Chang'an, Qi led troops and put down the revolt.

sentences.zh: 會韓絳城綏州不利，起亦罷知江寧府。

translations.literal: When Han Jiang's fortification of Sui Prefecture went badly, Qi was also dismissed and made prefect of Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Jiang's attempt to fortify Sui Prefecture failed, Qi was dismissed and made prefect of Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 入知吏部流內銓。

translations.literal: He entered the capital to direct the Ministry of Personnel's inner roster.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital to head the Ministry of Personnel's inner roster.

sentences.zh: 奉使契丹，至王庭，其位著乃與夏使等，起曰：「彼陪臣爾，不當與王人齒。」

translations.literal: On embassy to the Khitan, at the royal court their seating placed him with the Xia envoy and others; Qi said: "They are mere retainers and should not rank with the sovereign's men."
translations.idiomatic: On embassy to the Khitan, at court his seat was set with the Xia envoy and others; Qi protested, "They are only retainers and should not rank with the sovereign's envoys."

sentences.zh: 辭不就列，遂升東朝使者，自是為定制。

translations.literal: He refused to take his place and was then seated with the eastern-dynasty envoys; this thereafter became fixed practice.
translations.idiomatic: He refused his assigned place and was seated with the Song envoys instead, and this became permanent practice.

sentences.zh: 六年，拜天章閣待制、知桂州。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was made Hanlin academician awaiting orders and prefect of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was made Hanlin academician awaiting orders and prefect of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 自王安石用事，始求邊功，王韶以熙河進，章惇、熊本亦因此求奮。

translations.literal: From the time Wang Anshi held power the court began seeking frontier achievements; Wang Shao advanced through the Hexi River region, and Zhang Dun and Xiong Ben likewise sought to distinguish themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Once Wang Anshi took power the court began chasing frontier glory; Wang Shao advanced through the Hexi corridor, and Zhang Dun and Xiong Ben likewise sought distinction.

sentences.zh: 是時，議者言交阯可取，朝廷命蕭注守桂經略之。

translations.literal: At that time advisers said Jiaozhi could be taken; the court ordered Xiao Zhu to hold Guizhou and plan the campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Advisers then claimed Jiaozhi could be seized; the court ordered Xiao Zhu to hold Guizhou and direct the effort.

sentences.zh: 注蓋造謀者也，至是，復以為難。

translations.literal: Zhu had been the original plotter; now he again declared it difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu, who had first devised the scheme, now declared it too difficult.

sentences.zh: 起言：「南交小醜，無不可取之理。」

translations.literal: Qi said: "The petty southern foe of Jiaozhi—there is no reason it cannot be taken."
translations.idiomatic: Qi said, "Jiaozhi is a trifling southern enemy—there is no reason it cannot be taken."

sentences.zh: 乃以起代注，遂一意事攻討。

translations.literal: Qi was sent to replace Zhu and then devoted himself wholly to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Qi replaced Zhu and threw himself entirely into the offensive.

sentences.zh: 妄言密受旨，擅令疆吏入溪洞，點集土丁為保伍，授以陣圖，使歲時肄習。

translations.literal: He falsely claimed secret imperial orders, on his own authority sent frontier officials into stream valleys, mustered native levies into baojia militia, gave them battle diagrams, and had them drill each year.
translations.idiomatic: He falsely claimed secret orders, sent frontier officials into tribal valleys on his own authority, mustered native levies into militia companies, taught them battle formations, and required annual drill.

sentences.zh: 繼命指使因督餫鹽之海濱，集舟師寓教水戰。

translations.literal: He then ordered agents to supervise salt transport on the coast and gathered boatmen to drill in naval warfare.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent agents to oversee coastal salt transport and gathered boatmen for naval drill.

sentences.zh: 故時交人與州縣貿易，悉禁止之。

translations.literal: All trade between Jiaozhi and the prefectures and counties was forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: All trade between Jiaozhi and local prefectures was banned.

sentences.zh: 於是交阯益貳，大集兵丁謀入寇。

translations.literal: Jiaozhi therefore grew more disloyal, massed troops, and planned invasion.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaozhi grew more hostile, gathered troops, and planned an invasion.

sentences.zh: 蘇緘知邕州，以書抵起，請止保甲，罷水運，通互市。

translations.literal: Su Jian, prefect of Yongzhou, wrote Qi urging him to halt the baojia militia, end water transport, and reopen mutual trade.
translations.idiomatic: Su Jian, prefect of Yongzhou, wrote urging Qi to halt the militia, end water transport, and reopen border trade.

sentences.zh: 起不聽，劾緘沮議，起坐邊議罷。

translations.literal: Qi would not listen, impeached Jian for obstructing policy, and Qi was dismissed from frontier planning.
translations.idiomatic: Qi refused, impeached Jian for obstruction, and Qi was removed from frontier planning.

sentences.zh: 命劉彝代之以守廣，日遏絕其表疏，於是交人疑懼，率眾犯境，邊陷廉、白、欽、邕四州，死者數十萬人。

translations.literal: Liu Yi was ordered to replace him and guard Guang, daily blocking memorials from below; the Jiaozhi people grew fearful and suspicious, mustered forces, invaded, and the border lost Lian, Bai, Qin, and Yong prefectures with hundreds of thousands dead.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi replaced him to guard Guang, daily suppressing reports from below; the Jiaozhi people grew fearful, rose in force, invaded, and Lian, Bai, Qin, and Yong fell with hundreds of thousands dead.

sentences.zh: 事聞，貶起團練使，安置郢州，徙越，又徙秀而卒。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported Qi was demoted to militia training commissioner and settled at Yingzhou, moved to Yue, then to Xiu, and died there.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached court Qi was demoted to militia training commissioner and exiled to Yingzhou, then Yue, then Xiu, where he died.

sentences.zh: 起生平喜談兵，嘗以兵法謁范仲淹，仲淹器其材，注孫武書以自見，卒用此敗。

translations.literal: Qi all his life loved to discuss warfare; he once presented military texts to Fan Zhongyan, who valued his talent; he annotated Sun Wu to display his learning and in the end failed through this.
translations.idiomatic: Qi loved military talk all his life; he once presented strategy to Fan Zhongyan, who admired his talent; he annotated Sunzi to show his learning—and was ruined by it.

sentences.zh: 劉彝，字執中，福州人。

translations.literal: Liu Yi, style name Zhizhong, was a man of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi, whose style name was Zhizhong, came from Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 幼介特，居鄉以行義稱。

translations.literal: As a child he was independent; in his village he was known for righteous conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a boy he was self-contained; in his home district he was praised for moral conduct.

sentences.zh: 從胡瑗學，瑗稱其善治水，凡所立綱紀規式，彝力居多。

translations.literal: He studied under Hu Yuan, who praised his skill in water control; in all regulations and standards established, Yi contributed the greater part.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under Hu Yuan, who praised his mastery of hydraulics; Yi did most of the work in every regulation Hu established.

sentences.zh: 第進士，為邵武尉，調高郵簿，移朐山令。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi, became Wei of Shaowu, was transferred to registrar of Gaoyou, and moved to magistrate of Qushan.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi, served as Wei of Shaowu, became registrar of Gaoyou, and was made magistrate of Qushan.

sentences.zh: 治簿書，恤孤寡，作陂池，教種藝，平賦役，抑奸猾，凡所以惠民者無不至。

translations.literal: He managed documents, cared for orphans and widows, built reservoirs, taught planting, equalized taxes and labor, and curbed the cunning and violent—every means of benefiting the people he pursued without fail.
translations.idiomatic: He managed records, cared for widows and orphans, built reservoirs, taught farming, equalized taxes and labor service, and suppressed sharp dealers—every way to help the people he pursued exhaustively.

sentences.zh: 邑人紀其事，目曰「治範」。

translations.literal: The townspeople recorded his deeds and called them "Models of Governance."
translations.idiomatic: Locals recorded his deeds under the title "Models of Governance."

sentences.zh: 熙寧初，為制置三司條例官屬，以言新法非便罷。

translations.literal: Early in Xining he was an official of the Fiscal Reform Commission and was dismissed for saying the New Policies were inconvenient.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xining he served on the Fiscal Reform Commission and was dismissed for criticizing the New Policies.

sentences.zh: 神宗擇水官，以彝悉東南水利，除都水丞。

translations.literal: The emperor chose a water official; because Yi knew southeastern hydraulics thoroughly he was made director of waterways.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong chose a hydraulics expert; knowing Yi's mastery of southeastern waterworks, he made him director of waterways.

sentences.zh: 久雨汴漲，議開長城口，彝請但啟楊橋斗門，水即退。

translations.literal: After long rain the Bian River rose; some proposed opening the Changcheng outlet; Yi asked only to open the Yangqiao sluice gate and the water at once receded.
translations.idiomatic: After prolonged rain the Bian flooded; some wanted to open the Changcheng outlet; Yi urged opening only the Yangqiao sluice, and the water immediately fell.

sentences.zh: 為兩浙轉運判官。

translations.literal: He became transport judge of the Two Zhe circuits.
translations.idiomatic: He was made transport judge on the Two Zhe circuit.

sentences.zh: 知虔州，俗尚巫鬼，不事醫藥。

translations.literal: As prefect of Qianzhou the custom favored shamans and ghosts and rejected medicine.
translations.idiomatic: At Qianzhou the people favored shamans and spirits and shunned physicians.

sentences.zh: 彝著《正俗方》以訓，斥淫巫三千七百家，使以醫易業，俗遂變。

translations.literal: Yi wrote Correct Customs Formulas for instruction, expelled three thousand seven hundred licentious shamans, and made them take up medicine instead; the custom was transformed.
translations.idiomatic: Yi wrote Correct Customs Formulas to instruct the people, expelled three thousand seven hundred illicit shamans, and made them practice medicine instead, and customs changed.

sentences.zh: 加直史館，知桂州。

translations.literal: He was given direct appointment to the historiographical institute and made prefect of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He received direct appointment to the historiographical institute and became prefect of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 禁與交人互市，交阯陷欽、廉、邕三州，坐貶均州團練副使，安置隨州。

translations.literal: He forbade mutual trade with the Jiaozhi people; Jiaozhi seized Qin, Lian, and Yong prefectures; he was demoted to deputy militia training commissioner of Junzhou and settled at Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He banned trade with Jiaozhi; Jiaozhi captured Qin, Lian, and Yong; he was demoted to deputy militia training commissioner of Junzhou and exiled to Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 又除名為民，編隸涪州，徙襄州。

translations.literal: He was further stripped of office and made a commoner, registered at Fuzhou, and moved to Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was further stripped of rank, made a commoner, registered at Fuzhou, and moved to Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 元祐初，復以都水丞召還，病卒於道，年七十。

translations.literal: Early in the Yuanyou reign he was again summoned as director of waterways but died on the road at seventy.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuanyou he was again summoned as director of waterways but died on the journey at seventy.

sentences.zh: 著《七經中義》百七十卷，《明善集》三十卷，《居陽集》三十卷。

translations.literal: He authored Interpretations of the Seven Classics in one hundred seventy scrolls, Collected Writings on Understanding Goodness in thirty scrolls, and Collected Writings from Juyang in thirty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Interpretations of the Seven Classics in one hundred seventy juan, Collected Writings on Understanding Goodness in thirty juan, and Collected Writings from Juyang in thirty juan.

sentences.zh: 論曰：兵，凶器也，雖聖人猶曰未學。

translations.literal: The commentary says: Arms are an inauspicious instrument; even the sage said he had not mastered them.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: War is an instrument of ill omen; even the sage said he had not fully learned it.

sentences.zh: 輕敵寡謀，鮮有不自焚者。

translations.literal: Those who despise the enemy and plot lightly rarely do not burn themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Those who slight the foe and plot rashly seldom escape self-destruction.

sentences.zh: 永樂之陷，安南之畔，死者百萬，罹禍甚慘，良由數人者不自量度，以開邊釁。

translations.literal: The fall of Yongle and the revolt in Annam killed a million men with calamity most cruel—all because several men would not measure themselves and opened border strife.
translations.idiomatic: The fall of Yongle and the Annamese rebellion killed a million people in appalling disaster, because a handful of men would not gauge their strength and opened border war.

sentences.zh: 禧、稷、永能之死，宜矣。

translations.literal: The deaths of Xi, Ji, and Yongneng were fitting.
translations.idiomatic: The deaths of Xi, Ji, and Yongneng were deserved.

sentences.zh: 起執議益堅，妄意輕舉，雖貶官莫贖其責。

translations.literal: Qi clung all the more to his views, acted on reckless intent, and though demoted could not expiate his guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Qi clung ever harder to his views, acted with reckless presumption, and even demotion could not absolve him.

sentences.zh: 彝不能行所學，而規規然蹈前車之轍，以濟其過，烏得無罪？

translations.literal: Yi could not put his learning into practice but pedantically followed the tracks of the cart before him to compound the fault—how could he be without guilt?
translations.idiomatic: Yi could not apply what he had learned but pedantically retraced the ruts of his predecessors to worsen the harm—how could he be blameless?

sentences.zh: 熊本，字伯通，番陽人。

translations.literal: Xiong Ben, style name Botong, was a man of Poyang.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong Ben, whose style name was Botong, came from Poyang.

sentences.zh: 兒時知學，郡守范仲淹異其文。

translations.literal: As a child he loved learning; the prefect Fan Zhongyan was struck by his writing.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning as a boy; Prefect Fan Zhongyan was impressed by his essays.

sentences.zh: 進士上第，為撫州軍事判官，稍遷秘書丞、知建德縣。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi with high standing, became military judge of Fuzhou, and was gradually promoted to secretary and magistrate of Jiande County.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi with high standing, became military judge of Fuzhou, and rose to secretary and magistrate of Jiande County.

sentences.zh: 縣令墳包魚池為窪田，本弛以與民。

translations.literal: The county magistrate had turned fishponds in ancestral graves into low fields; Ben released them to the people.
translations.idiomatic: The previous magistrate had turned grave-side fishponds into paddy; Ben restored them to the people.

sentences.zh: 熙寧初，上書言：「陛下師用賢傑，改修法度，得稷、禼、皋、夔之佐。」

translations.literal: Early in Xining he memorialized: "Your Majesty takes worthy men as teachers, reforms laws and institutions, and has helpers like Ji, Xie, Gao, and Kui."
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xining he memorialized, "Your Majesty employs worthy men as teachers, reforms laws and institutions, and has aides like Ji, Xie, Gao, and Kui."

sentences.zh: 由是提舉淮南常平、檢正中書禮房事。

translations.literal: Through this he was made supervisor of the Huainan ever-normal granary and rectifier of the Secretariat rites office.
translations.idiomatic: He was thereby made supervisor of the Huainan ever-normal granary and rectifier of the Secretariat rites office.

sentences.zh: 六年，瀘州羅、晏夷叛，詔察訪梓、夔，得以便宜治夷事。

translations.literal: In the sixth year the Luo and Yan tribes of Luzhou rebelled; he was ordered to inspect Zi and Kui and given discretionary power to handle tribal affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year the Luo and Yan tribes of Luzhou rebelled; he was sent to inspect Zi and Kui with discretionary authority over tribal affairs.

sentences.zh: 本嘗通判戎州，習其俗，謂：「彼能擾邊者，介十二村豪為鄉導爾。」

translations.literal: Ben had once been vice prefect of Rongzhou and knew their customs; he said: "Those who can trouble the border are only the twelve village magnates who serve as guides."
translations.idiomatic: Having served as vice prefect of Rongzhou he knew their ways and said, "Only the twelve village magnates who act as guides can stir border trouble."

sentences.zh: 以計致百餘人，梟之瀘川，其徒股栗，願矢死自贖。

translations.literal: By stratagem he brought in more than a hundred men and executed them at Luzhou; their followers trembled and vowed to die to atone.
translations.idiomatic: By ruse he lured in more than a hundred men and beheaded them at Luzhou; their followers shook with fear and vowed to die in atonement.

sentences.zh: 本請於朝，寵以刺史、巡檢之秩，明示勸賞，皆踴躍順命，獨柯陰一酋不至。

translations.literal: Ben requested of the court that they be honored with prefect and inspector ranks as a clear reward; all leapt to obey except one Ke Yin chieftain who did not come.
translations.idiomatic: He asked the court to honor them with prefect and inspector ranks as open encouragement; all eagerly submitted except one Ke Yin chieftain who stayed away.

sentences.zh: 本合晏州十九姓之眾，發黔南義軍強弩，遣大將王宣、賈昌言率以進討。

translations.literal: Ben combined the masses of the nineteen clans of Yan Prefecture, sent the Qiannan militia crossbowmen, and dispatched the generals Wang Xuan and Jia Changyan to lead the advance.
translations.idiomatic: Ben rallied the nineteen Yan clans, mobilized Qiannan militia crossbowmen, and sent generals Wang Xuan and Jia Changyan to lead the attack.

sentences.zh: 賊悉力旅拒，敗之黃葛下，追奔深入。

translations.literal: The rebels resisted with all their strength; he defeated them below Huangge and pursued deep into their territory.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fought with their full strength; he routed them at Huangge and drove deep into their country.

sentences.zh: 柯陰窘，乞降，盡籍丁口、土田及其重寶善馬，歸之公，上受貢職。

translations.literal: Ke Yin was cornered and begged to surrender, registering all men, land, and his treasures and fine horses to the state; the court accepted his tribute duties.
translations.idiomatic: Cornered, Ke Yin sued for peace, registering population, land, treasure, and fine horses to the state, and the court accepted his tribute obligations.

sentences.zh: 於是烏蠻羅氏鬼主諸夷皆從風而靡，願世為漢官奴。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Wuman Ghost Lords of the Luo clan and all the tribes followed the wind and submitted, wishing to be slaves of Han officials for generations.
translations.idiomatic: Then the Wuman Ghost Lords and other tribes submitted in waves, declaring they wished to be Han officials' bondsmen forever.

sentences.zh: 遷刑部員外郎、集賢殿修撰、同判司農寺。

translations.literal: He was moved to vice director of the Ministry of Punishments, collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and concurrent director of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice director of punishments, collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and concurrent director of the revenue ministry.

sentences.zh: 神宗勞之曰：「卿不傷財，不害民，一旦去百年之患，至於檄奏詳明，近時鮮儷焉。」

translations.literal: The emperor praised him: "You neither wasted treasure nor harmed the people, yet in a day removed a century-old scourge; your proclamations and memorials are detailed and clear—rarely matched in recent times."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong praised him: "You spent no treasure and harmed no people, yet in a day removed a century-old menace; your dispatches are lucid and precise—seldom matched in our day."

sentences.zh: 賜三品服。

translations.literal: He was granted third-rank robes.
translations.idiomatic: He received third-rank court robes.

sentences.zh: 西南用兵蠻中始此。

translations.literal: Southwestern campaigns among the tribes began with this.
translations.idiomatic: This marked the beginning of southwestern warfare among the tribal peoples.

sentences.zh: 蔡京時為秀州推官，本言其學行純茂，練習新法，薦為幹當公事。

translations.literal: Cai Jing was then push officer of Xiuzhou; Ben said his learning and conduct were pure and that he was practiced in the New Policies, and recommended him as duty officer.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Jing was then a Xiuzhou push officer; Ben praised his learning and conduct and knowledge of the New Policies and recommended him as a duty officer.

sentences.zh: 河、湟初復，本為秦鳳路都轉運使。

translations.literal: When the He and Huang regions were first recovered, Ben became chief transport commissioner of the Qinfeng circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When the He-Huang region was first recovered, Ben became chief transport commissioner on the Qinfeng circuit.

sentences.zh: 熙河法禁闊略，蓄積不支歲月，本奏省冗官百四十員，歲減浮費數十萬。

translations.literal: The Hexi regulations were loose and stores could not last a year; Ben memorialized to cut one hundred forty redundant officials and reduce floating expenses by several hundred thousand a year.
translations.idiomatic: Hexi regulations were lax and stores would not last a year; Ben proposed cutting one hundred forty redundant posts and saving several hundred thousand in annual waste.

sentences.zh: 渝州南川獠木鬥叛，詔本安撫。

translations.literal: The Moudou tribe of Nanchuan in Yuzhou rebelled; Ben was ordered to pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: The Moudou tribesmen of Nanchuan in Yuzhou rebelled, and Ben was ordered to pacify them.

sentences.zh: 本進營銅佛壩，抗其尤，焚積聚，以破其黨。

translations.literal: Ben advanced to camp at Tongfo Dam, resisted their leaders, burned their stores, and broke their faction.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to Tongfo Dam, struck at their leaders, burned their stockpiles, and shattered their party.

sentences.zh: 木斗氣索，舉溱州地五百里來歸，為四砦九堡，建銅佛壩為南平軍。

translations.literal: Moudou's spirit was broken; he surrendered five hundred li of Qin Prefecture territory, which was made four stockades and nine forts, and Tongfo Dam was established as Nanping Army.
translations.idiomatic: Moudou's resistance collapsed; he yielded five hundred li of Qin territory, organized into four stockades and nine forts, with Tongfo Dam made Nanping Army.

sentences.zh: 初，熟獠王仁貴以木斗親繫獄，本釋其縛置麾下，至是推鋒先登。

translations.literal: Earlier the assimilated tribesman Wang Rengui had been imprisoned for kinship with Moudou; Ben released his bonds and placed him in his command; now he led the assault in the van.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rengui, an assimilated tribesman jailed for ties to Moudou, was freed and taken into Ben's service; now he led the vanguard assault.

sentences.zh: 大臣議加本天章閣待制，帝曰：「本之文，朕所自知，當典書命。」

translations.literal: The great ministers discussed making Ben Hanlin academician awaiting orders; the emperor said: "Ben's writing—I know it myself—he should draft imperial edicts."
translations.idiomatic: Ministers proposed making Ben a Hanlin academician; the emperor said, "I know Ben's prose myself—he should draft edicts."

sentences.zh: 遂知制誥。

translations.literal: He was then made drafter of imperial edicts.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed drafter of imperial edicts.

sentences.zh: 帝數稱其文有體，命院吏別錄以進。

translations.literal: The emperor often praised the structure of his writing and ordered Academy clerks to copy selections for presentation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor often praised his literary structure and ordered separate copies submitted to the throne.

sentences.zh: 又上疏云：「天下之治，有因有革，期於趣時適治而已。

translations.literal: He further memorialized: "The governance of the realm has grounds for continuity and for change; the aim is only to suit the times and secure good order.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized again: "Governance must both continue and change; the goal is only timely order suited to the age.

sentences.zh: 議者猥用持盈守成之說，文苟簡因循之治，天下之吏因以安常習故為俗，奮言納忠者，悠悠之徒相與蹙額盱衡而詆罵之。

translations.literal: Advisers vulgarly applied the doctrine of holding full and guarding the achieved, ornamenting negligent rule that follows precedent; officials everywhere took ease in custom as their way, and those who spoke boldly in loyalty were mocked by the multitude with knitted brows and sidelong glances.
translations.idiomatic: Critics clung to 'hold what is full, guard what is achieved,' praising negligent precedent; officials coasted on habit, while men who spoke loyal truth were sneered at by the crowd.

sentences.zh: 陛下出大號，發大政，可謂極因革之理。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has issued a great proclamation and launched great policies—this may be called the utmost of continuity and change.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has proclaimed great reforms—this is continuity and change at its fullest.

sentences.zh: 然改制之始，安常習故之群圜視四起，交讙而合譟，或諍於廷，或謗於市，或投劾引去者，不可勝數。

translations.literal: Yet at the start of reform the company wedded to custom glared from all sides, joined in clamor, wrangling in court, slandering in the markets, or submitting resignations without number.
translations.idiomatic: Yet at reform's start the old guard glared from every side, clamored together, quarreled in court, slandered in markets, and resigned in droves.

sentences.zh: 陛下燭見至理，獨立不奪，今雖少定，彼將伺隙而逞。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has illumined the highest principle and stood firm without wavering; though things are somewhat settled now, they will watch for openings to act.
translations.idiomatic: You have seen the deepest principle and stood unmoved; though things seem calmer, they will watch for a chance to strike.
