sentences.zh: 願陛下深念之，勿使譟讙之眾有以窺其間，而終萬世難就之業，天下幸甚。」

translations.literal: I beg Your Majesty to ponder this deeply, not let the clamorous multitude spy a gap, and bring to completion the enterprise hard to achieve for ten thousand generations—the realm would be greatly fortunate."
translations.idiomatic: Ponder this deeply, Majesty, lest the noisy opposition find a crack, and finish the work of ages—the empire would be blessed."

sentences.zh: 本之意，專以媚王安石也。

translations.literal: Ben's intent was solely to flatter Wang Anshi.
translations.idiomatic: Ben's aim was simply to flatter Wang Anshi.

sentences.zh: 范子淵創浚河之役，文彥博爭之，命本行視，議如彥博。

translations.literal: Fan Ziyuan initiated the river-dredging project; Wen Yanbo opposed it; Ben was ordered to inspect on site and sided with Yanbo.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Ziyuan launched a river-dredging project; Wen Yanbo objected; Ben inspected the site and agreed with Yanbo.

sentences.zh: 安石白出本分司西京。

translations.literal: Anshi had him sent out to the Western Capital branch office.
translations.idiomatic: Anshi had him posted to the Western Capital branch office.

sentences.zh: 居三年，起知滁州，改廣州，召為工部侍郎。

translations.literal: After three years he was recalled as prefect of Chuzhou, changed to Guangzhou, and summoned as vice minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: After three years he was recalled as prefect of Chuzhou, then Guangzhou, then summoned as vice minister of works.

sentences.zh: 宜州蠻擾邊，道除龍圖閣待制、知桂州。

translations.literal: When Yizhou tribes troubled the border he was made Dragon Diagram academician awaiting orders and prefect of Guizhou on the way.
translations.idiomatic: When Yizhou tribes raided the frontier he was made Dragon Diagram academician and prefect of Guizhou en route.

sentences.zh: 至則諭溪洞酋長，戒邊吏勿生事，請選將練兵代戍，益市馬以足騎兵，宜州遂無事。

translations.literal: On arrival he instructed stream-valley chieftains, warned border officials not to provoke trouble, asked to select generals to train troops to replace garrisons, and increased horse purchases to fill the cavalry; Yizhou was thereafter untroubled.
translations.idiomatic: He instructed tribal chiefs, warned border officers against provocation, sought trained replacements for garrisons, and bought horses to fill the cavalry; Yizhou was quiet thereafter.

sentences.zh: 民蔡寶㻇扇龍蕃與峒戶相仇殺，欲引兵致討以為功。

translations.literal: The man Cai Baoheng incited Long Fan and cave households to mutual killing, wishing to lead troops to attack and win merit.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Baoheng stirred Long Fan and cave people to slaughter one another, hoping to win glory by leading troops against them.

sentences.zh: 本質之色動，縛而投之海。

translations.literal: Ben saw his true intent and had him bound and cast into the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Ben read his intent, had him bound, and thrown into the sea.

sentences.zh: 蠻夷以為神。

translations.literal: The tribes took this for divine.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes regarded it as supernatural.

sentences.zh: 諜告交人明年將入寇，使者實其言，詔訪，本曰：「使者在道，安得此？

translations.literal: Spies reported the Jiaozhi people would invade next year; an envoy confirmed it; the emperor inquired; Ben said: "The envoy is still on the road—how could he know this?
translations.idiomatic: Spies said Jiaozhi would invade the next year; an envoy confirmed it; when the court asked, Ben said, "The envoy is still traveling—how could he know?

sentences.zh: 藉使有謀，何自先知之？」

translations.literal: Even if they had a plot, how could he know beforehand?"
translations.idiomatic: Even if they plotted, how could he foresee it?"

sentences.zh: 已而果妄。

translations.literal: And so it proved false.
translations.idiomatic: It proved false.

sentences.zh: 是時，既以順州賜李乾德，疆畫未正，交人緣是輒暴勿陽地而逐儂智會。

translations.literal: At that time Shun Prefecture had been granted to Li Qiande but the boundary was not fixed; the Jiaozhi people therefore seized Wuyang territory and drove out Nong Zhihui.
translations.idiomatic: Shun Prefecture had been granted Li Qiande but borders were unsettled; Jiaozhi seized Wuyang lands and expelled Nong Zhihui.

sentences.zh: 智會來乞師，本檄問狀，乾德斂兵謝本，因請以宿桑八洞不毛之地賜之，南荒遂安。

translations.literal: Zhihui came begging for troops; Ben sent an order to investigate; Qiande withdrew his troops and apologized to Ben, then asked that the barren lands of the Susang eight caves be granted him, and the southern wilds were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Zhihui begged for aid; Ben demanded an accounting; Qiande withdrew and apologized, requesting the barren Susang eight caves, and the south was calmed.

sentences.zh: 轉運判官許彥先議通湖南鹽於西廣，計口授民，度可得息三十萬。

translations.literal: Transport judge Xu Yanxian proposed extending Hunan salt into western Guang, allotting by population, estimating a profit of three hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Transport judge Xu Yanxian proposed selling Hunan salt in western Guang by head count, expecting three hundred thousand profit.

sentences.zh: 本言：「桂管民貧地瘠，恐不堪命。」

translations.literal: Ben said: "The Guiguan people are poor and the land lean—I fear they cannot bear the burden."
translations.idiomatic: Ben said, "Guiguan is poor and thin-soiled—the people cannot bear it."

sentences.zh: 議遂格。

translations.literal: The plan was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The plan was shelved.

sentences.zh: 入為吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as vice minister of personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as vice minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 逾年，力請外，仍待制、知洪州。

translations.literal: After a year he strongly requested an outer post and was still academician awaiting orders as prefect of Hongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he begged for an outside post and remained academician awaiting orders at Hongzhou.

sentences.zh: 言者謂本棄八洞為失謀，奪一官，徙杭州、江寧府，再知洪州。

translations.literal: Critics said Ben had abandoned the eight caves through faulty planning; one rank was stripped; he was moved to Hangzhou and Jiangning, then again made prefect of Hongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Critics said abandoning the eight caves was Ben's blunder; he lost one rank, served Hangzhou and Jiangning, then Hongzhou again.

sentences.zh: 召還，卒於道。

translations.literal: Recalled, he died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to court, he died on the journey.

sentences.zh: 有文集、奏議共八十卷。

translations.literal: He left collected works and memorials totaling eighty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He left collected writings and memorials in eighty juan.

sentences.zh: 蕭注，字岩夫，臨江新喻人。

translations.literal: Xiao Zhu, style name Yanfu, was a man of Xinyu in Linjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Zhu, style name Yanfu, came from Xinyu in Linjiang.

sentences.zh: 磊落有大志，尤喜言兵。

translations.literal: He was bold and ambitious and especially loved to discuss warfare.
translations.idiomatic: He was bold and ambitious and especially loved to talk of war.

sentences.zh: 常言：「四方有事，吾將兵數萬，鼓行其間，戰必勝，攻必取，豈不快哉！」

translations.literal: He often said: "When trouble arises in the four directions I shall lead tens of thousands of troops marching in array—every battle won, every assault taken—how could that not be exhilarating!"
translations.idiomatic: He often boasted, "When the realm stirs I shall march tens of thousands in array—victory in every fight, conquest in every siege—what could be sweeter?"

sentences.zh: 舉進士，攝廣州番禺令。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi and acted as magistrate of Panyu in Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi and served as acting magistrate of Panyu in Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 儂智高圍州數月，方舟數百攻城南，勢危甚。

translations.literal: Nong Zhigao besieged the prefecture for months with hundreds of boats attacking the south wall; the situation was dire.
translations.idiomatic: Nong Zhigao besieged the city for months with hundreds of boats against the south wall; the peril was extreme.

sentences.zh: 注自圍中出，募海濱壯士，得二千人，乘大舶集上流，因颶風起，縱火焚賊舟，破其眾。

translations.literal: Zhu escaped the siege, recruited coastal stalwarts, got two thousand men, took large ships upstream, and when a hurricane rose set fire and burned the rebel boats, breaking their force.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu broke out, recruited coastal fighters, gathered two thousand men, sailed large ships upstream, and when a typhoon rose burned the rebel fleet and broke their army.

sentences.zh: 即日發縣門納援兵，民持牛酒、芻糧相繼入，城中人始有生意。

translations.literal: That same day he opened the county gates to admit relief troops; the people brought oxen, wine, fodder, and grain in succession, and life returned to the city.
translations.idiomatic: That day he opened the gates to relief troops; people brought oxen, wine, fodder, and grain in streams, and the city revived.

sentences.zh: 自是每戰以勝歸。

translations.literal: From then on he returned victorious from every battle.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth he returned victorious from every fight.

sentences.zh: 蔣偕上其功，擢禮賓副使、廣南駐泊都監。

translations.literal: Jiang Jie reported his merit and he was promoted to vice envoy of the Office of Ceremonial Guests and Guangnan garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Jie reported his deeds and he was made vice ceremonial envoy and Guangnan garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 賊還據邕管，余靖患其嘯誘諸洞，以屬注。

translations.literal: The rebels still held Yong and Guan; Yu Jing feared they would incite the caves and entrusted Zhu.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels still held Yong and Guan; Yu Jing feared they would stir the caves and put Zhu in charge.

sentences.zh: 注挺身入蠻中，施結恩信。

translations.literal: Zhu went in person among the tribes and bestowed favor and trust.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu went in person among the tribes, winning them with grace and trust.

sentences.zh: 狄青師次賓州，召會諸將，疑注倚賊聲勢為奸利，欲誅之。

translations.literal: When Di Qing's army halted at Binzhou he summoned the generals, suspected Zhu of using the rebels' power for illicit profit, and wished to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: Di Qing halted at Binzhou, summoned generals, suspected Zhu of profiteering through the rebels' power, and meant to kill him.

sentences.zh: 注覺，託為遊辭，不肯往。

translations.literal: Zhu perceived this, pleaded illness as excuse, and would not go.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu sensed it, pleaded illness, and refused to attend.

sentences.zh: 賊破，青始聞注前功，以知邕州。

translations.literal: After the rebels were broken Qing first learned of Zhu's earlier merit and made him prefect of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels fell Qing learned of Zhu's earlier service and made him prefect of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 智高走大理國，母與二弟寓特磨道。

translations.literal: Zhigao fled to Dali; his mother and two younger brothers stayed on the Temo route.
translations.idiomatic: Zhigao fled to Dali; his mother and two brothers remained on the Temo route.

sentences.zh: 注帥師往討，獲一裨將。

translations.literal: Zhu led troops to attack and captured a deputy commander.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu led troops out, capturing a deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 引致臥內，與之語，具得賊情，悉擒送闕下。

translations.literal: He brought him into his chamber and talked with him, learning the full rebel situation, and captured and sent them all to court.
translations.idiomatic: He questioned him in private, learned the rebels' full situation, and sent all captives to court.

sentences.zh: 拜西上閤門副使。

translations.literal: He was made western upper gate vice envoy.
translations.idiomatic: He was made western upper gate vice envoy.

sentences.zh: 募死士使入大理取智高，至則已為其國所殺，函首歸獻。

translations.literal: He recruited daredevils to enter Dali and seize Zhigao; on arrival he had already been killed by that state; they brought his head boxed as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: He sent daredevils into Dali for Zhigao; he was already dead there; they brought back his head in a box.

sentences.zh: 轉為使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to envoy.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to envoy.

sentences.zh: 居邕數年，陰以利啖廣源群蠻，密繕兵甲，乃上疏曰：「交阯雖奉朝貢，實包禍心，常以蠶食王土為事。

translations.literal: Residing at Yong several years he secretly fed the Guangyuan tribes with profit and secretly repaired arms, then memorialized: "Jiaozhi though paying court tribute truly harbors treacherous intent and constantly nibbles at imperial territory.
translations.idiomatic: At Yong for years he secretly bribed Guangyuan tribes and armed his men, then wrote, "Jiaozhi pays tribute but harbors treachery and constantly eats away imperial soil.

sentences.zh: 往天聖中，鄭天益為轉運使，云責其擅賦雲河洞。

translations.literal: In the Tiansheng era Zheng Tianyi as transport commissioner had charged them with levying taxes on their own in Yunhe Cave.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tiansheng, transport commissioner Zheng Tianyi had rebuked their unauthorized levies in Yunhe Cave.

sentences.zh: 今雲河乃落蠻數百里，蓋年侵歲吞，馴致於是。

translations.literal: Now Yunhe has fallen to the tribes for several hundred li—year by year encroachment brought it to this.
translations.idiomatic: Now Yunhe lies in tribal hands for hundreds of li—years of nibbling brought this.

sentences.zh: 臣已盡得其要領，周知其要害。

translations.literal: I have fully grasped their essentials and know their vital points.
translations.idiomatic: I know their essentials and their weak points.

sentences.zh: 今不取，異日必為中國憂。

translations.literal: If we do not take it now, another day it will trouble China.
translations.idiomatic: If we do not seize it now, it will trouble China later.

sentences.zh: 願馳至京師，面陳方略。」

translations.literal: I wish to hurry to the capital and present strategy in person."
translations.idiomatic: I beg to rush to court and lay out strategy face to face."

sentences.zh: 未報，而甲洞申紹泰犯西平，五將被害。

translations.literal: Before reply came, the Jiadong chieftain Shen Shaotai attacked Xiping and five generals were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Before an answer came, Jiadong chief Shen Shaotai attacked Xiping and five generals died.

sentences.zh: 諫官論注不法致寇，罷為荊南鈐轄、提點刑獄。

translations.literal: Remonstrance officials charged Zhu's lawlessness had brought the raid; he was dismissed as Jingnan deputy commissioner and judicial intendant.
translations.idiomatic: Censors blamed Zhu's misconduct for the raid; he was demoted to Jingnan deputy commissioner and judicial intendant.

sentences.zh: 李師中又劾其沮威嗜利，略智高閹民為奴，發洞丁采黃金無帳籍可考。

translations.literal: Li Shizhong further impeached him for curbing prestige and craving profit, seizing Zhigao's castrated tribesmen as slaves, and sending cave levies to mine gold without records.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shizhong further charged him with crushing authority for gain, enslaving Zhigao's castrated followers, and sending cave levies to mine gold without accounts.

sentences.zh: 中使按驗頗有實，貶泰州團練副使。

translations.literal: Palace agents investigated and found substance; he was demoted to deputy militia training commissioner of Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Palace agents found the charges largely true; he was demoted to deputy militia training commissioner of Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 淮南轉運使言：「注椎牛屠狗，招集遊士，部勒為兵，教之騎射，請徙大州以縻之。」

translations.literal: The Huainan transport commissioner said: "Zhu butchers oxen and dogs, gathers wandering bravos, drills them as soldiers, and teaches mounted archery—please move him to a large prefecture to restrain him."
translations.idiomatic: The Huainan transport commissioner said Zhu butchered and gathered bravos, drilled them in archery, and asked he be moved to a large prefecture to restrain him."

sentences.zh: 詔改鎮南軍節度副使。

translations.literal: An edict changed him to deputy military commissioner of Zhennan Army.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made him deputy military commissioner of Zhennan Army.

sentences.zh: 近臣有訟注廣州功者，起為右監門將軍、邠州都監。

translations.literal: A courtier sued on Zhu's Guangzhou merit; he was raised to right gate general and Binzhou garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: A courtier pleaded Zhu's Guangzhou service; he was made right gate general and Binzhou garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 熙寧初，以禮賓使知寧州。

translations.literal: Early in Xining he was ceremonial envoy and prefect of Ningzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xining he was ceremonial envoy and prefect of Ningzhou.

sentences.zh: 環慶李信之敗，列城皆堅壁，注獨啟關夜宴如平時。

translations.literal: After Li Xin's defeat in Huan and Qing all walled cities barred their gates; Zhu alone opened his and feasted at night as in peacetime.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Xin's defeat on the Huan-Qing frontier every city shut its gates; Zhu alone opened his and feasted at night as if at peace.

sentences.zh: 復閤門使，管幹麟府軍馬。

translations.literal: He was again made gate envoy and managed Linfu army horses.
translations.idiomatic: He was again gate envoy in charge of Linfu cavalry.

sentences.zh: 辭云：「身本書生，差長拊納，不閑戰鬥，懼無以集事。」

translations.literal: He declined, saying: "I am fundamentally a scholar, only somewhat skilled in winning people—I am unpracticed in battle and fear I cannot accomplish the task."
translations.idiomatic: He declined: "I am a scholar at heart, only skilled in winning people over—I am no fighter and fear failure."

sentences.zh: 時有言交人挫於占城，眾不滿萬，可取也。

translations.literal: At the time some said the Jiaozhi people had been humbled by Champa and numbered fewer than ten thousand and could be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Some then said Jiaozhi, beaten by Champa, had fewer than ten thousand men and could be taken.

sentences.zh: 遂以注知桂州。

translations.literal: Zhu was therefore made prefect of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu was therefore made prefect of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 入覲，神宗問攻取之策，對曰：「昔者臣有是言，是時溪洞之兵，一可當十；

translations.literal: On audience the emperor asked strategy for attack; he replied: "Formerly I said this, but then stream-valley troops counted one for ten;
translations.idiomatic: At audience Shenzong asked how to attack; Zhu replied, "I once said so, but then stream-valley warriors counted ten for one;

sentences.zh: 器甲堅利，親信之人皆可指呼而使。

translations.literal: armor and weapons were sharp, and trusted men could all be summoned and sent.
translations.idiomatic: arms were keen, and trusted men obeyed at a word.

sentences.zh: 今兩者不如昔，交人生聚教訓十五年矣，謂之『兵不滿萬』，妄也。」

translations.literal: now both are inferior to before; the Jiaozhi people have gathered and trained for fifteen years—calling them 'fewer than ten thousand' is false."
translations.idiomatic: Now both are worse; Jiaozhi has trained fifteen years—to call them 'under ten thousand' is nonsense."

sentences.zh: 既至桂，種酋皆來謁。

translations.literal: Once he reached Guizhou all tribal chiefs came to audience.
translations.idiomatic: At Guizhou every tribal chief came to call.

sentences.zh: 注延訪山川曲折，老幼安否，均得其歡心，故李乾德動息必知之。

translations.literal: Zhu inquired after the twists of mountains and rivers and whether old and young were safe, winning all their hearts; therefore Li Qiande's every move was known to him.
translations.idiomatic: He asked after terrain and families, winning every heart, so Li Qiande's every move reached him.

sentences.zh: 然有獻征南策者，輒不聽。

translations.literal: Yet when anyone offered plans to conquer the south he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he refused every plan to conquer the south.

sentences.zh: 會沈起以平蠻自任，帝使代注而罷，注歸，卒於道，年六十一。

translations.literal: When Shen Qi took pacifying the tribes upon himself the emperor had him replace Zhu and dismiss him; Zhu returned and died on the road at sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: When Shen Qi styled himself tribal pacifier the emperor replaced Zhu with him; Zhu went home and died on the road at sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 詔優錄其子，賻絹三百。

translations.literal: An edict favored his sons and granted three hundred bolts of silk for funeral expenses.
translations.idiomatic: The court favored his sons and granted three hundred bolts of silk for the funeral.

sentences.zh: 注有膽氣，嗜殺，而能相人。

translations.literal: Zhu had courage, loved killing, and could read men's faces.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu was fearless, bloodthirsty, and could read faces.

sentences.zh: 自陝西還，帝問注：「韓絳為安撫使，施設何如？」

translations.literal: Returning from Shaanxi the emperor asked Zhu: "How does Han Jiang fare as frontier commissioner?"
translations.idiomatic: Returning from Shaanxi the emperor asked Zhu, "How does Han Jiang perform as frontier commissioner?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「廟算深遠，臣不能窺。

translations.literal: He replied: "The plan in the temple is far-reaching—I cannot see into it.
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Court strategy is far beyond me.

sentences.zh: 然知絳當位極將相。」

translations.literal: Yet I know Jiang will reach the utmost of generals and ministers."
translations.idiomatic: Yet I know Jiang will rise to the highest rank."

sentences.zh: 帝喜曰：「果如卿言，絳必成功。」

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and said: "If it is as you say, Jiang is sure to succeed."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said gladly, "If so, Jiang will succeed."

sentences.zh: 問王安石，曰：「安石牛目虎顧，視物如射，意行直前，敢當天下大事。

translations.literal: Asked about Wang Anshi, he said: "Anshi has ox eyes and a tiger's gaze, views things as if shooting, goes straight ahead by intent, and dares undertake the great affairs of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Asked about Wang Anshi, he said, "Anshi has ox eyes and a tiger's stare, sees like an archer, drives straight ahead, and dares shoulder the empire's great tasks.

sentences.zh: 然不如絳得和氣為多，惟氣和能養萬物爾。」

translations.literal: Yet he is not so harmonious as Jiang; only harmony can nourish the ten thousand things."
translations.idiomatic: Yet he lacks Jiang's harmony; only harmony nourishes all things."

sentences.zh: 王韶為建昌參軍，注曰：「君他日類孫沔，但壽不及。」

translations.literal: Wang Shao was a Jiancang staff officer; Zhu said: "You will one day resemble Sun Hao, but your lifespan will not match his."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shao was a Jiancang staff officer; Zhu said, "You will one day resemble Sun Hao, but you will not live as long."

sentences.zh: 後皆如其言。

translations.literal: Later both proved as he said.
translations.idiomatic: Later events proved him right on both counts.

sentences.zh: 陶弼，字商翁，永州人。

translations.literal: Tao Bi, style name Shangweng, was a man of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Bi, whose style name was Shangweng, came from Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 少俶儻，放宕吳中。

translations.literal: In youth he was bold and unrestrained, roaming freely in Wu.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was bold and free-spirited, wandering the Wu region.

sentences.zh: 行山間，有雙鯉戲溪水上，佇觀之。

translations.literal: Walking in the mountains he saw two carp sporting on the stream and stopped to watch.
translations.idiomatic: Walking in the hills he saw two carp playing in a stream and stopped to watch.

sentences.zh: 傍一老父顧曰：「此龍也，行且鬥，君宜亟去。」

translations.literal: An old man beside him said: "Those are dragons; they are about to fight—you should leave at once."
translations.idiomatic: An old man nearby said, "Those are dragons about to fight—you should leave at once."

sentences.zh: 去百步許，雷大震而雨，岸圮木拔。

translations.literal: A hundred paces on, thunder crashed and rain fell; the bank collapsed and trees were uprooted.
translations.idiomatic: A hundred paces on, thunder crashed and rain poured; the bank gave way and trees were torn up.

sentences.zh: 又出大雲，倉卒遇風暴怒，二十七艘同時溺，獨弼舟得濟，人以是異之。

translations.literal: Again at sea great clouds rose and he suddenly met a violent storm; twenty-seven boats sank together, yet Bi's alone reached shore—people regarded this as extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: At sea again, storm clouds rose and a sudden gale sank twenty-seven boats at once, yet Bi's alone survived—people took it as a sign.

sentences.zh: 一見丁謂，謂妻以宗女，因從學兵法，能持論縱橫。

translations.literal: On one meeting with Ding Wei, Wei gave him his clanswoman in marriage; he then studied military strategy and could argue with sweeping force.
translations.idiomatic: Meeting Ding Wei once, Wei gave him a clanswoman in marriage; he studied strategy and could argue with sweeping force.

sentences.zh: 慶曆中，楊畋討湖南徭，弼上謁，畋授之兵使往襲，大破之。

translations.literal: In the Qingli era Yang Tian quelled the Hunan Yao; Bi presented himself; Tian gave him troops for a raid and he inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qingli era Yang Tian campaigned against Hunan Yao; Bi sought him out, was given troops for a raid, and won a great victory.

sentences.zh: 以功得陽朔主簿。

translations.literal: For merit he was made chief clerk of Yangshuo.
translations.idiomatic: For this he was made chief clerk of Yangshuo.

sentences.zh: 儂智高犯南海，畋為安撫使，辟參軍謀。

translations.literal: When Nong Zhigao invaded the Southern Sea, Tian was frontier commissioner and took Bi as staff planner.
translations.idiomatic: When Nong Zhigao invaded the south, Tian as frontier commissioner made Bi his planning aide.

sentences.zh: 使下英江會諸將議擊，未至，智高解去。

translations.literal: He was sent down the Ying River to meet the generals to plan an attack; before he arrived Zhigao had withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: Sent down the Ying River to coordinate generals for an attack, he arrived after Zhigao had already withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 弼舍舟，從其徒數十人，間關步出赴畋。

translations.literal: Bi left his boat and with several dozen followers made his way overland through hardship to reach Tian.
translations.idiomatic: He abandoned his boat and with several dozen men made a hard overland march to Tian.

sentences.zh: 次臨賀，大將蔣偕適戰死，餘眾畏亡將被誅，多降賊。

translations.literal: At Linhe the great general Jiang Jie had just died in battle; the remaining troops feared execution for losing their commander and many surrendered to the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: At Linhe General Jiang Jie had just fallen; the survivors feared punishment for his death and many went over to the rebels.

sentences.zh: 弼數與之遇，亟矯畋命揭榜道上，諭使歸，許以不死，凡得千五百人。

translations.literal: Bi met them repeatedly; he forged Tian's orders and posted placards on the road telling them to return, promising they would not die—and recovered fifteen hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: Bi met them again and again, forged Tian's orders, posted placards promising amnesty, and recovered fifteen hundred men.

sentences.zh: 府罷，調陽朔令。

translations.literal: When the prefecture was disbanded he was transferred to magistrate of Yangshuo.
translations.idiomatic: When the command was dissolved he became magistrate of Yangshuo.

sentences.zh: 課民植木官道旁，夾數百里，自是行者無夏秋暑暍之苦，它郡縣悉效之。

translations.literal: He ordered the people to plant trees along the official road for several hundred li; travelers thereafter suffered no summer heat or autumn thirst, and other prefectures and counties all imitated this.
translations.idiomatic: He had trees planted along the post road for hundreds of li, sparing travelers summer heat and autumn thirst; other counties copied him.

sentences.zh: 攝興安令。

translations.literal: He acted as magistrate of Xing'an.
translations.idiomatic: He served as acting magistrate of Xing'an.

sentences.zh: 移書說桂守蕭固浚靈渠以通漕，不聽；

translations.literal: He wrote persuading the Gui prefect Xiao Gu to dredge the Spirit Canal for transport grain, but Gu would not listen;
translations.idiomatic: He urged Gui Prefect Xiao Gu to dredge the Ling Canal for grain transport, but Gu refused;

sentences.zh: 至李師中，卒浚之。

translations.literal: when Li Shizhong came he finally dredged it.
translations.idiomatic: when Li Shizhong arrived he finally completed the dredging.

sentences.zh: 師征安南，饋餉於是乎出，大為民利。

translations.literal: When the army campaigned against Annam supplies could then issue forth—a great benefit to the people.
translations.idiomatic: When troops marched on Annam, supplies could flow through it—a great public benefit.

sentences.zh: 知賓、容、欽三州，換崇儀副使，遷為使，知邕州。

translations.literal: He governed Bin, Rong, and Qin prefectures, exchanged posts to vice envoy of the Honored Ceremonies, was promoted to envoy, and made prefect of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Bin, Rong, and Qin, became vice ceremonial envoy, then envoy and prefect of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 邕經儂寇，井隧蕩然，人不樂其生。

translations.literal: Yong had suffered the Nong raids; wells and paths were ruined and people despaired of life.
translations.idiomatic: Yong had been ravaged by the Nong rebels; infrastructure lay in ruins and people despaired.

sentences.zh: 弼綏輯惠養，至忘其勤。

translations.literal: Bi soothed and nurtured them until they forgot their hardships.
translations.idiomatic: Bi soothed and nurtured them until they forgot their suffering.

sentences.zh: 諸峒獻土物求內附，弼降意撫答，謝其贄，皆感悅無犯邊者。

translations.literal: The caves presented local products seeking inner submission; Bi humbly received and answered them, declining their gifts, and all were moved to joy and did not trouble the border.
translations.idiomatic: Cave peoples brought tribute seeking submission; Bi received them humbly, declined gifts, and they were so moved that none raided the border.

sentences.zh: 邕地卑下，水易集，夏大雨彌月，弼登城以望，三邊皆漫為陂澤，亟窒垠江三門，諭兵民即高避害。

translations.literal: Yong lay low and water gathered easily; in summer a great rain lasted a month; Bi mounted the wall to look—on three sides all was flooded swamp; he quickly blocked the three gates of the Yuan River and told soldiers and civilians to seek high ground.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was low-lying and flood-prone; one summer month of rain flooded three sides; Bi mounted the walls, blocked the Yuan River's three gates, and ordered people to higher ground.

sentences.zh: 俄而水大至，弼身先版臿，召僚吏賦役，為土囊千餘置道上，水果從竇入，隨塞之。

translations.literal: Soon the water surged; Bi himself took up shovel and basket, summoned officials and laborers, made more than a thousand earth bags on the roads; water entered through holes and was blocked as it came.
translations.idiomatic: When the flood peaked Bi took shovel in hand, rallied officials and laborers, laid a thousand earth bags along the roads, and plugged every breach as water entered.

sentences.zh: 城雖不壞，而人皆乏食，則為發廩以振於內，方舟以饁於外，水不及女牆者三板，旬有五日乃退，公私一無所失亡。

translations.literal: Though the city was not destroyed all lacked food; he opened granaries within and sent boats with food from without; water did not reach three planks below the parapet; after fifteen days it receded with no public or private loss.
translations.idiomatic: The city held, but food ran short; he opened granaries and sent supply boats; water stayed three planks below the parapet; after fifteen days it fell without loss.

sentences.zh: 自橫、潯以東數州皆沒。

translations.literal: From Heng and Xun eastward several prefectures were submerged.
translations.idiomatic: East from Heng and Xun several prefectures were drowned.

sentences.zh: 弼久於邕，請便郡，徙鼎州。

translations.literal: Bi had long been at Yong and requested a nearer prefecture; he was moved to Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Long service at Yong led him to request a nearer post; he was moved to Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 章惇經理五溪蠻事，薦為辰州，遷皇城使。

translations.literal: Zhang Dun managed the Wuxi tribal affairs and recommended him for Chenzhou; he was made imperial city envoy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dun, managing Wuxi tribes, recommended him for Chenzhou; he became imperial city envoy.

sentences.zh: 降北江彭師宴，授忠州刺史。

translations.literal: He subdued Peng Shiyan of the Northern River and was made prefect of Zhongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He subdued Peng Shiyan of the Northern River and was made prefect of Zhongzhou.

sentences.zh: 郭逵南征，轉弼康州團練使，復知邕州。

translations.literal: When Guo Kui campaigned south he transferred Bi to militia training commissioner of Kangzhou and again made him prefect of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Under Guo Kui's southern campaign Bi became militia training commissioner of Kangzhou and again prefect of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 民再罹禍亂，散匿山谷，弼率百騎深入左江峒，民知其至，扶老攜幼以歸。

translations.literal: The people had twice suffered calamity and hid in the mountains; Bi led a hundred horsemen deep into the Zuo River caves, and when they knew he had come they brought old and young home.
translations.idiomatic: Twice ravaged, people hid in the hills; Bi led a hundred horsemen into the Zuo River caves, and families came home at his arrival.

sentences.zh: 逵帥官軍臨富良江，使弼殿。

translations.literal: Kui led the government army to the Fu River; he made Bi command the rear guard.
translations.idiomatic: Kui brought the imperial army to the Fu River and put Bi in charge of the rear.

sentences.zh: 交人納款，逵欲班師，恐為所襲。

translations.literal: The Jiaozhi people submitted; Kui wished to withdraw the army but feared ambush.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaozhi submitted; Kui wanted to withdraw but feared attack.

sentences.zh: 乃以計夜起，軍不整，騎步相蹈藉亂行。

translations.literal: He therefore rose at night by stratagem; the army was not in order and cavalry and infantry trampled one another in disorder.
translations.idiomatic: He broke camp at night by ruse; troops were disorderly and cavalry and foot tangled in chaos.

sentences.zh: 賊隔江陰伺覘，知弼殿，弗敢追。

translations.literal: The rebels watched from across the river in secret and, knowing Bi held the rear, did not dare pursue.
translations.idiomatic: Enemy scouts across the river saw Bi guarding the rear and dared not pursue.

sentences.zh: 弼申令帳下毋動，遲明，結隊徐行，逵賴以善還。

translations.literal: Bi ordered his camp not to move; at dawn he formed ranks and marched slowly; Kui returned safely thanks to this.
translations.idiomatic: Bi held his men still; at dawn he formed ranks and marched slowly, and Kui escaped safely.

sentences.zh: 建所得廣源峒為順州，桄榔為縣。

translations.literal: The captured Guangyuan caves were made Shun Prefecture and Kuanglang County.
translations.idiomatic: Captured Guangyuan caves became Shun Prefecture with Kuanglang County.

sentences.zh: 進弼西上閤門使，留知順州。

translations.literal: Bi was advanced to western upper gate envoy and left to govern Shun Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was made western upper gate envoy and left to govern Shun Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 州去邕二千里，多毒草瘴霧，戍卒死者什七八，弼亦疾甚，然蚤莫勞軍，視其良苦，意氣激揚，士莫不感泣，強奮起為用。

translations.literal: The prefecture was two thousand li from Yong, with many poisonous plants and miasma; seven or eight tenths of garrison soldiers died; Bi also grew very ill, yet morning and evening he labored for the army, watching their hardships, spirit high, and the men all wept and roused themselves to serve.
translations.idiomatic: Two thousand li from Yong, with poison and miasma, seven or eight in ten garrison troops died; Bi fell gravely ill yet still labored for the army morning and night until men wept and roused themselves.

sentences.zh: 交人襲取桄榔，揚聲欲圖州，獨難弼。

translations.literal: The Jiaozhi people raided Kuanglang and proclaimed they would take the prefecture, singling out Bi as the difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaozhi raided Kuanglang and vowed to take the prefecture, naming Bi as their obstacle.

sentences.zh: 弼素得人心，賊動息皆先知。

translations.literal: Bi had long won men's hearts; every enemy move was known to him beforehand.
translations.idiomatic: Bi had long won hearts; every enemy move reached him first.

sentences.zh: 獲間諜不殺，諭以逆順，縱之去，恩威兩施，以是終弼在不敢犯。

translations.literal: Captured spies he did not kill but instructed in right and wrong and released them; favor and awe together applied—therefore while Bi remained they did not dare offend.
translations.idiomatic: He spared spies, taught them loyalty and treason, and released them; mixing grace and terror, enemies dared not strike while he held the post.

sentences.zh: 加東上閤門使，未拜而卒。

translations.literal: He was given eastern upper gate envoy but died before investiture.
translations.idiomatic: He was to be eastern upper gate envoy but died before taking the seal.

sentences.zh: 詔錄其家五人。

translations.literal: An edict enrolled five of his family in office.
translations.idiomatic: The court enrolled five of his household in office.

sentences.zh: 弼能為詩，好士樂施，所得俸祿，悉以與人，家至貧不恤也。

translations.literal: Bi could write poetry, loved scholars, and delighted in giving; all salary he gave away, and his household was destitute without concern.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote poetry, loved scholars, and gave freely; he spent every salary and let his household grow poor without care.

sentences.zh: 既死，妻在鄉里，僦屋以居。

translations.literal: After death his wife in the countryside rented a house to live in.
translations.idiomatic: After his death his wife in the country rented a room to live in.

sentences.zh: 林廣，萊州人。

translations.literal: Lin Guang was a man of Laizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Guang came from Laizhou.

sentences.zh: 以捧日軍卒為行門，授內殿崇班，從環慶蔡挺麾下。

translations.literal: From a Pillar-of-the-Sun army soldier he became inner-palace honored ban and served under Cai Ting of Huan and Qing.
translations.idiomatic: Rising from a Pillar-of-the-Sun soldier to inner-palace honored ban, he served under Cai Ting on the Huan-Qing frontier.

sentences.zh: 李諒祚寇大順城，廣射中之。

translations.literal: When Li Liangzuo raided Dashun City Guang shot and hit him.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Liangzuo raided Dashun City, Guang's arrow struck him.

sentences.zh: 李信敗於荔原，廣引兵西入，破十二盤，攻白豹、金湯，皆先登。

translations.literal: After Li Xin was defeated at Liyuan, Guang led troops west, broke Twelve Passes, and attacked Baibao and Jintang, always first over the wall.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Xin's defeat at Liyuan, Guang marched west, took Twelve Passes, and stormed Baibao and Jintang, always first up the walls.

sentences.zh: 夜過洛河，夏人來襲，廣揚聲選強弩列岸側，實卷甲疾趨，夏人疑不敢渡。

translations.literal: Crossing the Luo River at night, Xia troops came to attack; Guang shouted that picked crossbowmen were lined on the bank while in fact he hurried on in armor; the Xia suspected and did not cross.
translations.idiomatic: Crossing the Luo by night as Xia attacked, Guang feigned strong crossbows on the bank while hurrying on in armor; the Xia suspected an ambush and did not ford.

sentences.zh: 嘗護中使臨邊，將及烏雞川，遽率眾循山行。

translations.literal: He once escorted a palace envoy to the border; nearing Wuji River he suddenly led his men along the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Escorting a palace envoy to the frontier, nearing Wuji River he suddenly led his men along the ridges.

sentences.zh: 道遇熟羌以險告，廣不答，夏人果伏兵於川，計不行而去。

translations.literal: He met assimilated Qiang who warned of danger; Guang did not answer; Xia had indeed laid ambush in the river valley and, the plan failing, withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Assimilated Qiang warned of danger; Guang ignored them; Xia had indeed ambushed the valley and withdrew when the ruse failed.

sentences.zh: 告者乃諜也。

translations.literal: The informant had been a spy.
translations.idiomatic: The informant had been a spy.

sentences.zh: 夏人圍柔遠城，廣止守，戒士卒即有變毋得輕動。

translations.literal: When the Xia besieged Rouyuan City Guang held defense only and warned the troops that if trouble arose they must not act rashly.
translations.idiomatic: When Xia besieged Rouyuan, Guang held the defense and forbade rash movement if trouble broke out.

sentences.zh: 火夜起積薪中，眾屯守自若。

translations.literal: Fire rose at night in the piled fuel; the troops guarded as usual.
translations.idiomatic: Night fire broke out in the fuel stacks; the garrison held steady.

sentences.zh: 明日，敵至馬平川，大持攻具來。

translations.literal: The next day the enemy reached Mapingchuan with great siege engines.
translations.idiomatic: Next day the enemy reached Mapingchuan with heavy siege gear.

sentences.zh: 廣被甲啟他門鼓而出，若將奪其馬，敵舍城救馬，廣復入，益修守備，夜募死士斫其營。

translations.literal: Guang donned armor, opened another gate, and drummed out as if to seize their horses; the enemy abandoned the city to save the horses; Guang re-entered, strengthened defenses, and at night sent daredevils to cut their camp.
translations.idiomatic: Guang armored, sallied from another gate as if to seize horses; foes abandoned the walls; he re-entered, strengthened defenses, and sent night raiders into their camp.

sentences.zh: 夏人數失利，始引退。

translations.literal: The Xia suffered repeated losses and began to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: After repeated losses the Xia began to pull back.

sentences.zh: 累遷禮賓使。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to ceremonial envoy.
translations.idiomatic: He rose repeatedly to ceremonial envoy.

sentences.zh: 韓絳奏為本道將。

translations.literal: Han Jiang memorialized him as a general of the circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Han Jiang recommended him as a circuit general.

sentences.zh: 慶兵據北城叛，廣在南城，望其眾進退不一，曰：「是不舉軍亂也。」

translations.literal: Qing troops held the north city in revolt; Guang was in the south city; seeing their masses advance and retreat unevenly he said: "This is not a whole-army mutiny."
translations.idiomatic: Qing mutineers held the north city while Guang was in the south; seeing uneven movement he said, "This is not a full-army revolt."

sentences.zh: 挺身縋城出其後，諭以逆順，皆投兵聽命。

translations.literal: He let himself down by rope from the wall behind them and instructed them in loyalty and treason; all cast down weapons and obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: He roped down behind them, preached loyalty and treason, and all threw down arms and obeyed.

sentences.zh: 出者才三百人，廣語餘眾曰：「亂者去矣，汝曹事我久，能聽命，不唯得活，仍有功。」

translations.literal: Only three hundred came out; Guang told the rest: "The rebels have gone; you have long served me—if you obey, you not only live but win merit."
translations.idiomatic: Only three hundred came out; he told the rest, "The rebels are gone—you who obey will live and even win reward."

sentences.zh: 得百餘人。

translations.literal: He got more than a hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: He won more than a hundred men.

sentences.zh: 激厲要束，使反攻城下兵，禽戮皆盡，遂平北城。

translations.literal: He roused and bound them, turned them to attack the troops below the wall, and captured and killed all; the north city was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: He rallied them, turned them on the mutineers below the wall, killed them all, and pacified the north city.

sentences.zh: 出追亂者，至石門山與之遇，諭之不肯降；

translations.literal: He pursued the rebels to Shimen Mountain and met them; he instructed them but they would not submit;
translations.idiomatic: Pursuing rebels to Shimen Mountain, he urged surrender in vain;

sentences.zh: 縱兵尾擊，敵知不得免，始請命。

translations.literal: he loosed troops to harry them; knowing escape was impossible they then begged for life.
translations.idiomatic: he harried them until, seeing no escape, they begged for mercy.

sentences.zh: 廣曰：「不從吾言，今窘而就死，非降也。」

translations.literal: Guang said: "You would not heed my words; now cornered you seek death—it is not submission."
translations.idiomatic: Guang said, "You refused my words; cornered now you beg for life—that is not surrender."

sentences.zh: 悉斬之。

translations.literal: He beheaded them all.
translations.idiomatic: He beheaded them all.

sentences.zh: 遷本路都監。

translations.literal: He was moved to circuit supervisory commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was made circuit supervisory commissioner.

sentences.zh: 詔入對，神宗獎金湯、石門之功，慰賜甚厚，將使開熙河。

translations.literal: Summoned for audience, Shenzong praised his Jintang and Shimen achievements and comforted and rewarded him richly, intending to send him to open the Hexi River region.
translations.idiomatic: At audience Shenzong praised Jintang and Shimen, rewarded him richly, and meant to send him to open the Hexi.

sentences.zh: 辭以不習洮、隴事，乃遷鈐轄使，還徙鄜延。

translations.literal: He declined, saying he was unpracticed in Tao and Long affairs, and was made deputy commissioner, then moved to Fuyan.
translations.idiomatic: He declined unfamiliarity with Tao and Long, was made deputy commissioner, then posted to Fuyan.

sentences.zh: 攻踏白城，功最，遷皇城使。

translations.literal: Attacking Tabai City his merit was greatest and he was made imperial city envoy.
translations.idiomatic: Attacking Tabai City he won top honors and became imperial city envoy.

sentences.zh: 進討洮羌，加帝御器械、環慶副都總管。

translations.literal: Advancing against Tao Qiang he was given imperial ordnance and made deputy overall commander of Huan and Qing.
translations.idiomatic: Campaigning against Tao tribes he received imperial ordnance and became deputy overall commander of Huan and Qing.

sentences.zh: 安南用師，詣闕請行。

translations.literal: When Annam was attacked he came to court requesting service.
translations.idiomatic: When war came to Annam he sought duty at court.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「南方卑濕。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The south is low and damp.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The south is low and damp.

sentences.zh: 知卿病足，西邊方開拓，宜復歸。」

translations.literal: Knowing your foot ailment, and with the west frontier opening, you should return there."
translations.idiomatic: Knowing your foot troubles, and with the western frontier opening, you should return west."

sentences.zh: 擢龍神衛四廂都指揮使、英州刺史。

translations.literal: He was raised to commander of the fourth wing of the Dragon Spirit Guard and prefect of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was made commander of the Dragon Spirit Guard's fourth wing and prefect of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 邊臣或言：「往者劉平因救鄰道戰沒，今宜罷援兵。」

translations.literal: Some frontier officials said: "Formerly Liu Ping died rescuing a neighboring circuit; now relief troops should be abolished."
translations.idiomatic: Some border officers said: "Formerly Liu Ping died while rescuing a neighboring circuit; relief troops should now be withdrawn."

sentences.zh: 廣曰：「此乃制賊長計也。

translations.literal: Guang said: "This is the long plan for controlling bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Guang said, "That is the long-term plan for controlling enemies.

sentences.zh: 使賊悉力寇一路，而他道不救，雖古名將亦無能為已。

translations.literal: Let the bandits use all their strength on one route while other routes send no aid—even ancient famous generals could do nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Let foes concentrate on one route while others send no aid—even famous ancient generals would fail.

sentences.zh: 平之所以敗，非出援罪。」

translations.literal: Ping's defeat was not the crime of going to aid."
translations.idiomatic: Ping's defeat was not because he went to the rescue."

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: The proposal was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 再轉步軍都虞候。

translations.literal: He was again made chief adjutant of the foot armies.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made chief adjutant of the foot armies.

sentences.zh: 韓存寶討瀘蠻乞弟，逗撓不進，詔廣代之。

translations.literal: Han Cunbao campaigned against the Lu tribal chief Qidi but stalled; Guang was ordered to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Han Cunbao stalled against Lu rebel Qidi; Guang replaced him.

sentences.zh: 廣至，閱兵合將，搜人材勇怯，三分之，日夕肄習，間椎牛享犒，士心皆奮。

translations.literal: On arrival he reviewed troops and generals, sorted men by courage and timidity into three parts, drilled them day and night, and occasionally feasted with oxen—morale soared.
translations.idiomatic: He reviewed troops, sorted men by courage, drilled them constantly, feasted them with slaughtered oxen, and morale soared.

sentences.zh: 遣使開曉乞弟，仍索所亡卒。

translations.literal: He sent envoys to persuade Qidi and demanded the lost soldiers back.
translations.idiomatic: He sent envoys to Qidi and demanded the lost soldiers.

sentences.zh: 乞弟歸卒七人，奏書降而身不至。

translations.literal: Qidi returned seven men and memorialized submission but did not come in person.
translations.idiomatic: Qidi returned seven men and wrote submission but did not appear.

sentences.zh: 乃決策深入，陳師瀘水，率將吏東鄉再拜。

translations.literal: He then decided on a deep advance, arrayed troops on the Lu River, and with generals and officials bowed east twice.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced deep, formed line on the Lu River, and bowed east with his officers.

sentences.zh: 誓之曰：「朝廷以存寶用兵亡狀，使我代之，要以必禽渠魁。

translations.literal: He swore: "The court, because Cunbao used the army badly, sent me to replace him and demands the rebel chief be taken.
translations.idiomatic: He swore, "The court sent me because Cunbao failed, and demands the rebel chief be taken.

sentences.zh: 今孤軍遠略，久駐賊境，退則為戮，冒死一戰，勝負未可知。

translations.literal: Now a lone army far from home, long stationed in enemy land—retreat means execution; risking death in one battle, victory is uncertain.
translations.idiomatic: A lone army deep in enemy country, retreat means death; one desperate battle may win or lose.

sentences.zh: 縱死，猶有賞，愈於退而死也。

translations.literal: Even if we die there is reward, better than retreating to die.
translations.idiomatic: Death may still bring reward, better than retreating to die.

sentences.zh: 與汝等戮力而進，可乎？」

translations.literal: Will you advance with all your strength?"
translations.idiomatic: Will you fight with all your strength?"

sentences.zh: 眾皆踴躍。

translations.literal: All leapt eagerly.
translations.idiomatic: All leapt to agree.

sentences.zh: 廣挾所得渠帥及質子在軍，而令以次酋護餉，以是入箐道而無鈔略之患。

translations.literal: Guang took captured chiefs and hostages with the army and had lesser chiefs guard supplies, and so entered the ravine paths without fear of raiders.
translations.idiomatic: Guang took captured chiefs and hostages with the army and had lesser chiefs guard supplies, entering ravine paths without raider trouble.

sentences.zh: 師行有二途，從納溪抵江門近而險，從寧遠抵樂共壩遠而平。

translations.literal: The army had two routes: from Naxi to Jiangmen was near but perilous; from Ningyuan to Legong Dam was far but level.
translations.idiomatic: Two routes existed: Naxi to Jiangmen was short but dangerous; Ningyuan to Legong Dam was long but easy.

sentences.zh: 蠻意官軍必出江門，盛兵阻隘；

translations.literal: The tribes expected the government army must use Jiangmen and massed troops to block the pass;
translations.idiomatic: Tribes expected troops at Jiangmen and massed to block the pass;

sentences.zh: 而師趨樂共，蠻不能支，皆遁去。

translations.literal: but the army hastened to Legong and the tribes could not hold and all fled.
translations.idiomatic: but the army took Legong, tribes could not hold, and all fled.

sentences.zh: 廣分兵繞帽溪，掩江門後，破其險，水際皆通行，益前進，每戰必捷。

translations.literal: Guang divided troops around Maoxi to strike behind Jiangmen, broke the defile, and the waterside was all passable; advancing further he won every battle.
translations.idiomatic: Guang sent troops around Maoxi to strike behind Jiangmen, opened the defile, and won every battle as he advanced.

sentences.zh: 次落婆遠，乞弟遣叔父阿汝約降求退舍，又約不解甲。

translations.literal: At Luopoyuan Qidi sent his uncle Ayue to feign surrender and ask the army to withdraw, also asking that armor not be removed.
translations.idiomatic: At Luopoyuan Qidi sent his uncle Ayue to feign surrender and demand withdrawal without disarming.

sentences.zh: 廣策其有異，除阜為壇，距中軍五十步，且設伏。

translations.literal: Guang judged there was trickery, cleared a mound for a platform fifty paces from headquarters, and set an ambush.
translations.idiomatic: Guang sensed treachery, built a platform fifty paces from camp, and laid an ambush.

sentences.zh: 明日，乞弟擁千人出降，匿弩士氈裘，猶豫不前謝恩。

translations.literal: Next day Qidi brought a thousand men to surrender, hiding crossbowmen in fur coats, hesitating and not advancing to give thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Next day Qidi brought a thousand men, crossbowmen hidden in fur coats, hesitating to approach.

sentences.zh: 廣發伏擊之，蠻奔潰，斬阿汝及大酋二十八人。

translations.literal: Guang sprang the ambush; the tribes fled in rout; Ayue and twenty-eight great chiefs were beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Guang sprang the ambush; tribes fled; Ayue and twenty-eight chiefs were beheaded.

sentences.zh: 乞弟以所乘馬授弟阿字，大將王光祖追斬之，軍中爭其屍，乞弟得從江橋下脫走。

translations.literal: Qidi gave his horse to his younger brother Azi; the great general Wang Guangzu pursued and killed him; the army fought over the corpse; Qidi escaped under Jiang Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Qidi gave his horse to his brother Azi; Wang Guangzu killed him; troops fought over the body; Qidi escaped under Jiang Bridge.

sentences.zh: 得其種落三萬，進次歸徠州，窮探巢穴，發故酋甫望箇恕塚。

translations.literal: Three tens of thousands of his tribes were taken; advancing to Guilaizhou they probed the nest, opening the tomb of the former chief Fuwang Gezhu.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty thousand tribesmen were taken; at Guilaizhou they probed deep, opening the tomb of former chief Fuwang Gezhu.

sentences.zh: 天寒，士多墮指，而乞弟竟不可得。

translations.literal: Heaven was cold and many soldiers lost fingers to frost, yet Qidi could not be got.
translations.idiomatic: Cold took many men's fingers to frostbite, yet Qidi could not be caught.

sentences.zh: 監軍先受密詔，聽引兵還，遂班師。

translations.literal: The supervising commissioner had first received a secret edict permitting withdrawal, and the army was withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: The supervising commissioner held a secret edict allowing withdrawal, and troops were pulled back.

sentences.zh: 拜衛州防禦使、馬軍都虞候。

translations.literal: He was made defense commissioner of Weizhou and chief adjutant of the horse armies.
translations.idiomatic: He was made defense commissioner of Weizhou and chief horse-army adjutant.

sentences.zh: 西兵未解，上疏求面陳方略。

translations.literal: Western troops were not yet dismissed; he memorialized asking to present strategy in person.
translations.idiomatic: With western troops still active he asked to present strategy in person.

sentences.zh: 及入見，言：「韓存寶雖有罪，功亦多，以今日朝廷待諸將，存寶不至死。」

translations.literal: On audience he said: "Though Cunbao was guilty, his merit was also great; with how the court now treats generals, Cunbao would not have had to die."
translations.idiomatic: At audience he said: "Though Cunbao was guilty, his merit was also great; with how the court now treats generals, Cunbao would not have had to die."

sentences.zh: 廣還部，至閿鄉，疽發斷頸卒，年四十八。

translations.literal: Guang returned to his post; at Wenxiang carbuncle broke his neck and he died at forty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: Returning to his post, at Wenxiang a carbuncle broke his neck and he died at forty-eight.

sentences.zh: 廣為人有風義，輕財好施，學通《左氏春秋》。

translations.literal: Guang was a man of moral bearing, light with wealth and generous, learned in the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: Guang was principled, generous with wealth, and versed in the Zuo Commentary.

sentences.zh: 臨事持重，長於料敵，以智損益《八陳圖》，又撰約束百餘條列上，邊地頗推行之。

translations.literal: In affairs he was weighty, skilled at reading the enemy, used wisdom to revise the Eight Formations, and drafted more than a hundred regulations submitted upward, widely applied on the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Weighty in action, skilled at reading enemies, he revised the Eight Formations by wit and drafted regulations widely used on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 其名聞於西夏。

translations.literal: His name was known in Western Xia.
translations.idiomatic: His name was known among the Western Xia.

sentences.zh: 秉常母梁氏將內侮，論中國將帥，獨畏廣，聞其南征，乃舉兵。

translations.literal: When Liang, mother of Bingchang, was about to trouble within, discussing Chinese commanders she alone feared Guang; hearing of his southern campaign she raised troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Bingchang's mother Lady Liang plotted within, she feared only Guang among Song commanders; hearing of his southern campaign she raised troops.

sentences.zh: 然在瀘以敕書招蠻，既降而殺之，此其短也。

translations.literal: Yet at Lu he summoned tribes by imperial writ, and after they submitted he killed them—this was his fault.
translations.idiomatic: Yet at Lu he summoned tribes by imperial writ and killed them after submission—his fault.

sentences.zh: 遄被惡疾死，或以為殺降之報雲。

translations.literal: Soon struck by a vicious illness and dead—some said it was retribution for killing those who had surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he died of a vicious illness—some called it retribution for killing submitters.

sentences.zh: 論曰：宋太宗既厭兵，一意安邊息民，海內大治。

translations.literal: The commentary says: After Emperor Taizong grew weary of war he devoted himself wholly to securing the border and resting the people, and the realm was greatly ordered.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: After Taizong tired of war he secured borders and rested the people, and the realm was greatly ordered.

sentences.zh: 真宗、仁宗深仁厚澤，涵煦生民，然仁文有餘，義武不足，蓋是時中國之人，不見兵革之日久矣。

translations.literal: Emperors Zhenzong and Renzong with deep benevolence and thick grace nurtured the living, yet benevolence and culture were abundant while martial righteousness was insufficient—for by then the people of China had not seen arms for long.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzong and Renzong nurtured the people with deep grace, yet culture outweighed martial vigor—for China had long been unaccustomed to war.

sentences.zh: 於是契丹、西夏起為邊患，乃不吝繒帛以成和好。

translations.literal: Then the Khitan and Western Xia arose as border troubles, and silk and brocade were not spared to secure peace.
translations.idiomatic: Then Khitan and Western Xia troubled the borders, and silk was lavished to buy peace.

sentences.zh: 神宗撫承平之運，銳焉有為，積財練兵，志在刷恥，故一時材智之士，各得暴其所長，以興立事功，若熊本、蕭注、陶弼、林廣實然。

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong inherited an age of peace, was keen to act, amassed wealth and drilled troops, his will set on wiping away shame; therefore men of talent and wisdom of the time each displayed their strengths to raise achievements—such as Xiong Ben, Xiao Zhu, Tao Bi, and Lin Guang, all outstanding.
translations.idiomatic: Shenzong inherited peace, amassed wealth, drilled troops, and sought to erase shame; so Xiong Ben, Xiao Zhu, Tao Bi, and Lin Guang each shone.

sentences.zh: 本、注起身科第，弼能詩好士，廣學通《左氏春秋》。

translations.literal: Ben and Zhu rose through the examinations; Bi could write poetry and loved scholars; Guang studied the Zuo Commentary.
translations.idiomatic: Ben and Zhu came through examinations; Bi wrote poetry and loved scholars; Guang mastered the Zuo Commentary.

sentences.zh: 昔孫權勸呂蒙學，文武豈二致哉！

translations.literal: Of old Sun Quan urged Lü Meng to study—are civil and martial truly two paths!
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan once urged Lü Meng to study—are wen and wu truly separate!

sentences.zh: 本上書以媚時相，廣之征蠻，發塚殺降，君子疵之。

translations.literal: Ben memorialized to flatter the chief minister; Guang's tribal campaign opened graves and killed submitters—gentlemen faulted them.
translations.idiomatic: Ben flattered the chief minister in memorials; Guang opened graves and killed submitters on campaign—gentlemen faulted both.
